Yes, but the buyer will want to see the rental license, the lease terms and proof the owner finished the city's rental training. A cash buyer can take the house with tenants in place or after they move out.

Do I need rental training to hold a St. Cloud rental license?

Yes. The city requires rental training as a condition of licensing. It is free and virtual, and you get three months from sign-up to finish.

Which county do I call about taxes on a St. Cloud house?

Call the county where your parcel sits, which is Stearns County for most of the city. A smaller part lies in Benton and Sherburne counties, so check the parcel before you call.

Is St. Cloud mostly renters or owners?

About half and half. Owners live in 48.6 percent of homes, so slightly more than half are rented.

How do I handle an inherited, vacant house in St. Cloud?

Look at the city's vacant property registration application first, then confirm who holds title and who can sign. Ask the county treasurer for the tax balance so the closing can be scheduled around it.

Which way of selling suits an Eagan house?

Sellers in Eagan generally pick between hiring an agent, handling the sale themselves, or accepting a cash offer. Condition, schedule and tenants decide which one makes sense.

A cash purchase can suit a rental owner facing a new license cycle, an owner moving on a short timeline, or a house still carrying decades-old finishes. This Dakota County suburb sits south of Saint Paul and borders the Minnesota River on the west. Drivers rely on Interstate 35E and Minnesota Highways 13, 55, 77 and 149. Population stands at 67,109 in the 2025 estimate, roughly 2.5 percent under the 2020 base. Eagan sits close to the Minneapolis-Saint Paul airport and the freeways, and warehouses and distribution centers cluster in the northern part of the city. A house near that area will draw a different buyer than one in a quiet residential pocket, so describe the setting honestly in your listing.

Does an Eagan rental license pass to the buyer?

No. The rental licensing ordinance dates from March 21, 2023. Each license covers one year and stays with the owner who applied, so a buyer must get a new one.

  • For 2026/27 a single-unit rental pays $165 a year plus a $25 application fee, and converting an owner-occupied home to a rental adds a $300 fee.
  • The city inspects each rental unit roughly every third year, or sooner after a complaint, and tenants must get at least 24 hours of notice.
  • Exemptions cover units rented to qualifying relatives of the owner, housing the state itself licenses, rooms within an owner-occupied home and contract-for-deed purchases recorded with Dakota County.

Renewing late adds 10 percent of the base fee in the first 30 days, 50 percent from 30 to 60 days and 100 percent after that. If tenants live in the house you are selling, call Community Development at 651-675-5681 first. Any buyer who keeps the tenants applies in their own name.

Permit and flood checks before a sale

The city issues permits on two tracks. Building permits are filed through the online ePermits system, and Building Inspections (651-675-5675) books 30-minute inspection slots on weekdays between 7:30 a.m. and 3:30 p.m. Projects that need no building permit get a zoning permit, which costs nothing.

Fences, patios, sport courts, driveway replacements, sidewalks, detached decks below 30 inches, one-story sheds up to 200 square feet, retaining walls under four feet and docks all fall under zoning permits. The city's property information page shows records and special assessments, and many files include scanned permits, inspection history and site surveys that let a buyer see what work was done.

On flood risk, every property is in FEMA Flood Zone X except those in Zone AE along the Minnesota River. The maps date from December 2, 2011, so call the Planning Department or FEMA to confirm an address.

Where an Eagan deed gets recorded

Only the Dakota County Administration Center in Hastings accepts deeds. You can book an appointment, or mail the deed to the Property Taxation and Records office, 1590 Highway 55, enclosing a cover letter, a stamped return envelope and your phone number.

Deed tax is 0.33 percent of the net price (Minnesota Statutes 287.21). A transfer deed must also include either a $54 well certificate or a signed well statement. Because most parcels here are abstract property, the title company searches the record before closing. Tax statements and valuation notices appear in the county's Property Information Search, and Property Taxation and Records takes questions at 651-438-4597.

Minnesota Statutes 513.55 also requires you to give the buyer a written list of known material facts before you sign.

Dakota County tax dates and payment

Property tax bills arrive in two halves, due May 15 and October 15. Paymentus handles online payments, charging 2.29 percent on cards, $2.95 on Visa debit or $0.35 for a bank transfer. Its phone line is 1-844-797-9075.

Counters at the Hastings, West St. Paul and Apple Valley buildings take payment on weekdays until 4:30 p.m. Mail must be postmarked by the due date. Owners without a mortgage company can sign up for free automatic payment.

A buyer who will live in the house should file the homestead application by December 31. Ask your closing agent how the year's tax gets prorated between you.

Getting an Eagan house ready for a buyer

Begin with documents: permit records and site surveys from the city's property page, plus the county tax statement. A tenant-occupied house also needs its rental license and newest inspection record. After that, choose how much work to do. Older finishes show better with fresh paint and serviced systems, though a cash buyer accepts the house untouched.

Get each offer in writing with a closing date. Then ask the title company for a payoff figure and for anything that might hold up recording. If a cash buyer is on the table, compare the final amount you would keep against a listing after repairs, showings and the wait for a lender, and pick the route that fits your calendar.

Will the buyer of my Eagan rental house inherit its license?

No transfer is possible. A license lasts one year, so the new owner applies for a fresh one. Community Development at 651-675-5681 can walk through the steps.

Which office takes a deed for recording in Dakota County?

The Property Taxation and Records office in Hastings. Book an appointment, or send the deed by mail to 1590 Highway 55 with a cover letter, return postage and a phone number.

Is my Eagan house in a flood zone?

Almost certainly not. Every property is in FEMA Flood Zone X except those in Zone AE along the Minnesota River. The maps date from 2011, so confirm an address with Planning or FEMA.

Does swapping out a fence or driveway before a sale need city approval in Eagan?

It needs a zoning permit, which is free. Fences, driveway replacements, patios, sheds up to 200 square feet and retaining walls under four feet are covered. Staff usually reply in two to five business days, and the Zoning Hotline is 651-675-5685.

When are Dakota County property taxes due?

Half on May 15 and half on October 15. You can pay online, in person or by mail, and a mailed payment counts if it is postmarked by the due date.

Fastest ways to sell a Burnsville house

A direct sale to an investor or cash buyer is usually the quickest route in Burnsville, since nobody is waiting on an appraisal or a mortgage approval. A regular listing takes longer and tends to net more. Selling on your own falls between the two.

Burnsville at a glance

Burnsville is in Dakota County, about 15 miles south of downtown Minneapolis, on a bluff above the Minnesota River. The township became a city in 1964, and growth was heavy through the 1990s. Rental licenses in Burnsville

The city licenses rentals of condominiums, townhouses, single-family homes, manufactured homes and multi-unit buildings, and it issues a license only after an initial inspection. Licenses renew on a quarterly schedule, with applications due a month before the expiration date. If you sell to someone who plans to rent the house out, these rules become part of their math.

  • Building and fire code inspections repeat every three years.
  • Landlords complete a manager training course before the license is issued.

A homeowner who rents a private home or an accessory dwelling unit through Airbnb or VRBO needs a short-term vacation rental license from Burnsville, renewed each year. Adjacent neighbors are notified as a courtesy, but the city will not deny the permit over an objection. A monthly lodging tax report is due within 25 days of month's end.

Accessory dwelling units are allowed on residential lots of at least 10,000 square feet, one per lot. The unit must be at least 300 square feet, have no more than two bedrooms, stay under half the size of the main house, sit on a permanent foundation, and add one off-street parking space. The owner has to live on the property at least 185 days a year, and the unit cannot be sold apart from the house. A garage can be converted only if a new garage of at least 440 square feet is built.

If the house you are selling has a backyard unit that was never permitted, call the Planning Division at 952-895-4455 before you list.

Permit history and the well statement

The city's public portal handles permits for roofing, siding, windows and doors, plumbing, mechanical, electrical and solar work, and anyone can search it for a property's history. Building Inspections answers questions at 952-895-4444. Pulling the record before you list shows whether the water heater, furnace or roof work over the years was permitted.

Minnesota Statutes section 103I.235 adds a duty at the sale. Before signing, you must tell the buyer in writing about any known wells on the property, or state that none are known. The deed has to carry the well statement or a well disclosure certificate, or the county will not record it. A separate written statement of known material facts is also required.

How recording works in Dakota County

Dakota County Property Taxation and Records records Burnsville deeds. In-person recording is by appointment at the Administration Center in Hastings. You can also mail documents to 1590 Highway 55, Hastings, MN 55033 with a cover letter, a self-addressed stamped envelope and a phone number. Originals come back in one to two weeks.

Most Dakota County property is Abstract rather than Torrens, which shapes how the title company searches the record. Every transfer deed needs a completed well disclosure certificate with a $54 fee, or one of the two certification statements printed on the deed. Questions go to 651-438-4597 or records@co.dakota.mn.us.

What a cash sale skips

A cash buyer works from the house as it stands, so you do not repaint, replace worn flooring or schedule open houses. There is no lender appraisal, which removes a common reason for deals to slip. The steps that remain are a price you agree on, a title search, signing the deed and disclosures, and recording in Dakota County.

Before you accept, ask the buyer for a closing date in writing and ask the title company what it needs from you. If the house is a former rental, bring the inspection history. If a mortgage remains, request a payoff statement so you know what you will walk away with.

Frequently asked questions

How soon can a cash sale close in Burnsville?

Mortgage payoffs, liens and Dakota County recording set the real pace, so get a date from the title company before you commit.

Do I need an inspection before selling my Burnsville house?

Not for an owner-occupied house. A former rental should come with its latest city inspection results, since rentals are inspected every three years. The city's permit search shows what other work was inspected.

Can the buyer rent out the house they buy from me?

Yes, after getting a Burnsville rental license, which requires an initial inspection and manager training. Relatives renting from the homeowner are one of the exceptions.

Which school district goes in a Burnsville listing?

Check the street first. Most addresses are in District 191, though some belong to District 196 or District 194, and a wrong name in an ad misleads buyers.

What does a Minnesota seller owe the buyer in writing?

A statement of known material facts that could significantly affect an ordinary buyer's use of the home, plus a statement about any wells. Give it honestly and in good faith.

Where Coon Rapids sits and why the address matters

Coon Rapids lies north of Minneapolis along the Mississippi and ranks second in size among Anoka County cities. The 2025 estimate counts 64,193 residents. U.S. Highway 10, Minnesota Highways 47 and 610 and Coon Rapids Boulevard carry most of the traffic, and the BNSF mainline cuts through town.

Expect a house beside a busy road to attract different shoppers than one on a quiet block by a park. Cenaiko Lake and Crooked Lake lie inside the city, and so do Bunker Hills Regional Park and Coon Rapids Dam Regional Park, so the exact address shapes how a sale goes.

Older houses and what buyers check

Coon Rapids was a village in 1952 and a city in 1959. Its population went from 14,931 in 1960 to 30,505 in 1970, 52,978 in 1990 and 63,599 at the 2020 census. A city that more than tripled between 1960 and 1990 has many houses that are now several decades old. Roofs, windows and mechanical systems deserve a look before you list.

Anoka-Hennepin District 11 runs the public schools. Coon Rapids Middle and Northdale Middle are the middle schools, and Coon Rapids High School is the public high school.

Coon Rapids ownership and income

Three of every four Coon Rapids homes are owner-occupied, and the middle owner-occupied value is about $306,000.

Rental and vacancy rules that affect a sale

The city keeps close watch on rentals and empty houses. Those rules can change your timeline and limit what a buyer may do with the property.

  • Every rental, single-family homes included, needs a city license before tenants move in. Processing takes about 4 to 6 weeks and includes a background check for each owner, a training certificate and a passed inspection.
  • Licenses renew every year, and starting in 2026 a late renewal brings a late fee. Inspections run on a 1, 2 or 3 year cycle based on results.
  • City Code 12-904 prohibits Airbnb, Vrbo and other short-term rentals, so a buyer cannot plan on that use.
  • A vacant house needs a vacant property permit. You submit the application with the fee, then call Building Inspections at 763-767-6476 to book a one-hour inspection.

If renters live in the house, phone the Housing Inspector at 763-767-6575 first. That call tells you where your license and inspection cycle stand.

Which repairs need a permit first?

Most of them do. The city lists windows, siding, roofing, electrical and plumbing work, drywall, demolition, framing, additions, garages, driveways, steps and decks as projects needing building permits, and some jobs also require a contractor.

Work done without a permit tends to surface during a buyer's inspection. Call the Inspections Division at 763-767-6476 before you hire anyone. A buyer who repairs the house after closing is the option when the work is more than you want to take on, with a price that accounts for it.

Recording a deed with Anoka County

The Anoka County Recorder accepts the deed for filing. State deed tax is 0.33 percent of net consideration under Minnesota Statutes 287.21. The recorder checks these items:

  • Sales of $3,000 or under pay a flat $1.65.
  • An agricultural conservation fee of $5 applies to transfer documents.
  • When an eCRV applies, its filing number is written on the deed.
  • The buyer's name and the tax statement address appear on the deed.
  • Delinquent tax on the parcel blocks recording until it is paid.
  • Every transfer deed needs a well disclosure certificate with a $54 fee, or the approved well statement printed on the deed.

Because most parcels in the county are abstract property, a full title search before the sale is the county's advice. Recording questions go to 763-323-5400 at the Government Center in Anoka. Statute 513.55 adds a duty to hand the buyer a written list of known material problems before signing.

Paying property tax when a house sells

Anoka County Property Records and Taxation collects the tax, and the county's property access site shows what is owed by parcel number or address. Call 763-323-5400 for the unpaid balance and the next due date. Your closing agent can explain the proration.

If you still owe tax before the sale, you have a few ways to pay. Online payment through PayAnokaCounty adds 2.6 percent for cards and Apple or Google Pay, or $3.50 for eCheck. A mailed check counts as on time only with a postmark dated by the due date. Paper checks paid at the Government Center counter, where weekday hours end at 4:30 p.m., carry no fee. The county's free Direct Payment Program pulls the amount from a bank account on the due date.

Which sale route fits a Coon Rapids house?

You can list with an agent, sell it yourself, or accept a cash offer. Repairs, your calendar and who lives in the house now should guide the choice.

A listing gives the most buyer exposure and suits a house in solid shape. A direct cash sale trades some price for speed and fewer conditions, which can help with a vacant house, a former rental that needs inspection work, or deferred repairs. Whichever you pick, pull together the rental license status, any open permits, the well disclosure and the tax balance first, since every buyer asks for them.

A short call list helps. The Housing Inspector can confirm where a rental stands, Building Inspections can tell you about permits and a vacant house, and the county can give the tax balance and recording needs. With those answers in hand, any buyer, cash or financed, can price the house quickly and set a closing date without surprises at the title company.

Frequently asked questions

Can I sell a Coon Rapids house with tenants living in it?

Yes, after you check the rental license. The city requires every rental, including single-family homes, to hold a city license and pass inspection, so call the Housing Inspector at 763-767-6575 to confirm where your license and inspection cycle stand.

Can a Coon Rapids buyer use the house for Airbnb stays?

No. City Code 12-904 bans Airbnb, Vrbo and other short-term rentals in Coon Rapids, so a buyer with that plan cannot count on it.

What is the state deed tax on a Coon Rapids sale?

It is 0.33 percent of net consideration, or $1.65 when the price is $3,000 or less. Anoka County adds a $5 conservation fee, and a well disclosure certificate costs $54 unless the approved well statement appears on the deed.

Does fixing up a Coon Rapids house before a sale require a permit?

For most projects, yes. Windows, siding, roofing, electrical, plumbing, drywall, decks, driveways and additions all need building permits. The Inspections Division at 763-767-6476 can say whether a particular job is covered.

How does the city treat a vacant house in Coon Rapids?

It requires a vacant property permit. Submit the application and fee at City Hall, then call Building Inspections at 763-767-6476 to schedule the one-hour inspection. Property Maintenance at 763-767-6470 takes complaints about empty properties.

Eden Prairie at a glance

Who buys in Eden Prairie?

Mostly people tied to the area's big employers and its school district. Optum, C.H. Robinson, Starkey and UNFI are among the larger employers in town.

Buyers at that income level expect a move-in ready house. Tired kitchens, deferred maintenance and work done without permits are the situations where owners turn to a direct purchase instead of a long listing.

Public schools in Eden Prairie

Eden Prairie Schools runs six elementary schools for pre-K through grade 5, one of them a Spanish immersion school, a single middle school for grades 6 to 8, and Eden Prairie High School. Minnesota open enrollment lets families choose schools outside their home district.

Alternatives include The International School of Minnesota and the Performing Institute of Minnesota Arts High School. Mention the district in any pitch to a buyer, since attendance is a fixed feature and families search by it.

What written disclosures does Minnesota ask of a seller?

Start with Minnesota Statutes 513.55, which has you tell the buyer in good faith about known facts that could significantly affect an ordinary buyer's use and enjoyment, before anyone signs a purchase agreement. Three narrower statutes add their own items.

  • Radon: test results, any mitigation system, the state warning and a Health Department booklet, under Section 144.496.
  • Wells: a statement that you know of none, or a description of each, under Section 103I.235.
  • Sewage: whether the property drains to a permitted facility, under Section 115.55.

Your agent or closing company can supply the standard forms for each.

Permits and a buyer's inspector

The city keeps permit files, and a buyer's inspector may ask for them. A building permit lapses after 180 days without work or an inspection, an accessory building over 200 square feet needs a permit, and a retaining wall over 4 feet tall needs a permit plus engineering.

Owners who live in their house may do their own work, with permits still required and natural gas work excluded. Minnesota requires builders, remodelers and roofers who work on homes to hold a state license, and the Department of Labor and Industry lets you verify a contractor.

If a finished basement, deck or roof lacks a closed permit, ask the building inspections office what closing it requires. Several permits must be applied for in person at the City Center on weekdays. Beginning January 1, 2027, paying by card adds a 2.95 percent charge, minimum $2.95, and bank transfers (EFT or ACH) skip it.

Keeping the house as a rental

Eden Prairie allows it, with a city rental license. Every rental property must hold that license and be inspected each year, and the number for rental questions is 952-949-8373. A rental that has lapsed or carries open corrections is easier to hand over to a buyer who accepts it as is than to fix first.

The city also offers a Housing Rehabilitation Loan Program and a First Time Homebuyer Program. Housing and Community Services, at 952-949-8394, can explain how those programs fit a buyer on your side of a sale.

Taxes and county paperwork after you accept an offer

Hennepin County bills the property tax in two installments, mid-May and mid-October. A date that lands on a weekend or holiday moves forward a business day. The tax information line is 612-348-3011, and Minnesota Statutes 279.01 sets late penalties.

The city assessor sends valuation and classification notices by mail each March, and an appraiser re-verifies physical details at least once in five years. Do not assume your homestead benefit follows the house. The buyer applies in their own name after moving in, and under Section 272.115 the assessor drops the old classification the next year unless the buyer qualifies. A homestead application must be made by December 31, covering occupancy from January 2 to December 31 of the year.

A sale above $3,000 also requires a value certificate for the auditor, and deed tax runs 0.33 percent of net consideration under Section 287.21.

A direct purchase removes the appraisal, the lender's conditions, the showings and the repair list. It does not remove the paperwork Minnesota requires. Which selling route suits an Eden Prairie house?

The answer turns on condition and timing.

  • Owner-handled sale: avoids a commission, and puts pricing, forms and negotiation on you.
  • Direct cash purchase: the buyer accepts the property as is, so repairs and open houses fall off the to-do list.

With home values this high, a few percentage points are large sums, so collect at least two written figures and compare what each leaves you after costs.

It depends on the route. A financed purchase moves at the pace of the appraisal and loan approval, while a cash purchase closes on a date set with the title company once ownership is clear. Recording at the county follows either one.

Must I repair my Eden Prairie house first?

No. Minnesota asks you to disclose known material facts, and it does not require repairs. Check for open or lapsed permits, since the city retains them and a buyer's inspector can look them up.

Does the buyer inherit my homestead classification?

No. Homestead is not passed on by the seller. The buyer files a homestead application after buying and moving in, in person at a Hennepin County service center or online.

Which taxes show up at an Eden Prairie closing?

The state deed tax, 0.33 percent of net consideration, travels with the deed, and a value certificate goes to the county. How the year's property tax is prorated depends on your purchase agreement.

Yes, provided the rental carries the city's license and yearly inspection. Call 952-949-8373 to check its status before marketing the property, and ask your closing agent how the lease and any deposit transfer.

Selling a house in Apple Valley

Apple Valley lies in northwestern Dakota County, so a sale involves the county's recording and tax offices in Hastings plus a few city rules on signs, parking and rentals. The paperwork looks much the same whichever way you sell.

Owners of homes that need work, carry unpaid tax or have tenants sometimes ask for cash offers, since the buyer takes the property as it stands. The Dakota County Community Development Agency also coordinates foreclosure assistance and home rehabilitation programs for Apple Valley, which is worth a call before you decide.

Apple Valley housing market

Apple Valley is mature and mostly built out. It has 55,248 residents, 2.0 percent fewer than the 56,374 counted in 2020, because the city has nearly used up its buildable land. The typical owner-occupied home was worth $370,400 for 2020 to 2024, and 73.4 percent of homes are owner-occupied. Median owner cost with a mortgage is $2,084 a month, median gross rent is $1,738, and households average 2.55 people. With little new land, resale houses make up most of what buyers see.

City rules a seller should know

Short term rentals of fewer than 30 days are not allowed in Apple Valley. A council ordinance clarified that they have never been a permitted use, so a house marketed to investors as an Airbnb or Vrbo property will not work as advertised. Owners of any residential rental property must register it with the city.

Yard and curb rules also come up during showings and open houses:

  • One for-sale sign per frontage, two on a corner lot, kept inside the property line and off the right of way, which usually reaches 13 feet behind the curb.
  • Open house signs may stand on city right of way within six blocks of the house, only on the day and during the hours of the open house.
  • Grass and weeds taller than eight inches are a public nuisance.
  • No more than four vehicles per home may be parked or stored outside, and all parking areas must be paved with concrete, asphalt or pavers.
  • Lawn watering is barred from 11 a.m. to 6 p.m. between May 1 and September 30, and public sidewalks must be cleared within 48 hours after a snowfall ends.

Trash containers go to the curb no earlier than 6 p.m. the night before pickup and come back by 10 p.m. on collection day. A garage sale may run three consecutive days, three times a year. Sheds of 200 square feet or less need no building permit, and fences over seven feet do. Code Enforcement at 952-953-2570 answers questions, and the Planning Department at 952-953-2575 handles setbacks.

Recording a deed in Dakota County

Deeds, mortgages and liens for every parcel are held by Dakota County Property Taxation and Records. Walk-in recording happens at the Administration Center, 1590 Highway 55 in Hastings, and requires an appointment. Mailed packets need the fees, a cover letter, a return envelope with postage and a phone number.

Land in Minnesota is recorded under two systems. With Abstract property, a title company searches the chain of documents. Torrens property instead carries a single certificate of title, close to final proof of who owns it. Abstract is the norm in Dakota County.

Wells matter at the recorder's counter. A transfer deed, a deed ending a contract for deed included, must come with a well disclosure certificate and a $54 fee unless the deed itself carries a statement. The statement can say the seller is unaware of any wells, or that the wells' number and status are unchanged from the last certificate on file. Staff do not assist with legal forms, so let the title company or an attorney prepare the paperwork.

How to pay Dakota County property tax

Real property tax is due May 15 and October 15, and the owner is responsible for timely payment whatever method is used. Manufactured homes follow August 31 and November 15, and farm second halves land on November 15.

Single online payments run through Paymentus, with a $100,000 ceiling per transaction, and you are done only when an emailed receipt shows up. Alternatives include the phone line at 1-844-797-9075, a mailed check to 1590 Highway 55, Hastings, MN 55033-2343 postmarked by the deadline, or a weekday visit to the Western Service Center in Apple Valley. The Hastings and West St. Paul offices also accept payments.

Free automatic withdrawals are open to owners without a mortgage-company escrow and without overdue tax. Cancellations need 15 days' notice before a due date. Statement and payoff questions go to 651-438-4576 or taxation@co.dakota.mn.us.

Before you list or accept a cash offer

Start with three calls. Ask Dakota County taxation at 651-438-4576 for the payoff on any unpaid tax. Call Code Enforcement at 952-953-2570 to learn whether any yard or parking issue is open on the property. If tenants live there, make sure the rental is registered with the city. Then give the title company or an attorney the well information so the deed can carry the right statement or certificate.

A cash buyer skips the lender, so the sale can move as quickly as the paperwork does. That means the tax payoff, the well statement and the recording appointment decide your closing date, and booking the recording appointment early removes the most common delay.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Apple Valley houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What to expect between offer and closing

After you accept an offer, the title company searches the chain of documents, which is the Abstract route used for most Dakota County parcels. It also requests the tax figures and reviews the deed for the well statement. You sign the deed and the disclosure paperwork at closing, and the title company then takes the deed to Property Taxation and Records for recording. Staff there do not help with legal forms, so any questions about wording go to the title company or an attorney.

If a buyer plans to rent the house, remind them that Apple Valley bars stays of fewer than 30 days and that any residential rental must be registered with the city. If the house is staying a rental under the new owner, give the buyer your tenant and registration details at the start. A buyer who pays cash will still want the same answers, and having them ready keeps the closing date from slipping. Check yard and parking items one more time before the final walkthrough, because a fresh notice from Code Enforcement can complicate a closing that is otherwise ready.

Frequently asked questions

Can I run an Airbnb in Apple Valley, MN?

No. Rentals under 30 days are barred, and the council's ordinance says they were never allowed. Longer-term rentals must be registered with the city.

Where is a deed recorded for an Apple Valley house?

Property Taxation and Records at the Dakota County Administration Center, 1590 Highway 55, Hastings. Appointments are available online, and mail recording is accepted.

What is a well disclosure certificate in Dakota County?

A filing that goes with each transfer deed for $54. A statement on the deed about unknown or unchanged wells can stand in for it.

How many cars can I park outside an Apple Valley home?

No more than four vehicles per dwelling unit, on a paved surface. An annual on-site parking permit allows two more, and the Planning Department at 952-953-2575 takes applications.

Which school district serves Apple Valley?

Independent School District 196. Some families opt into other districts under Minnesota's open enrollment statute.

Selling a house in Edina

Edina is a first-ring suburb of Minneapolis in Hennepin County, and it is almost fully built. The city covers about 16 square miles and is more than 95 percent developed, so nearly every sale is a resale of an existing house rather than new construction.

July 2025 population is 54,356. Median value of owner-occupied homes for 2020 to 2024 is $646,300, and 72.4 percent of households own. Those figures sit well above most Minnesota cities, and they shape what an Edina buyer expects to see: a sound structure, a clean record and few surprises at inspection.

How Edina's housing stock developed

Edina began as a farming and milling settlement along Minnehaha Creek in the 1860s, grew as a streetcar suburb, then expanded sharply in the 1950s and 1960s. Population jumped from 9,744 in 1950 to 30,482 in 1960 and 44,031 in 1970.

If your house dates from that burst, expect buyers and inspectors to ask about original windows, wiring, plumbing and basements. Houses in the older Country Club District and Morningside areas may draw questions about age and updates. Minnesota Highways 62 and 100 cut the city into four sections, and shoppers use Southdale Center and the 50th and France district, so a street's location affects who tours it.

Which school district do Edina buyers ask about?

Edina Public Schools, district 273, enrolls roughly 8,500 students. The district has one high school, Edina High School, two middle schools (South View and Valley View) and six elementary schools: Concord, Creek Valley, Cornelia, Highlands, Countryside and Normandale.

Because the district is a main reason families look at Edina, state the elementary attendance area plainly when you describe your house. Private options include Our Lady of Grace Catholic School and Golden Years Montessori.

Parks, transit and construction near your street

Edina's park department oversees 44 parks across more than 1,550 acres of parkland and open space, and the Braemar Ice Rink is part of the local hockey culture, so rink access comes up in conversations with buyers.

Commuters look at transit. Metro Transit runs daytime buses along France Avenue, and the Southdale Transit Center is one of the main hubs in the southwest metro. The Interstate 494 Edina and Richfield project is run by the Minnesota Department of Transportation, so check its page for construction that may affect a street near you. Mean travel time to work is 20.4 minutes.

What you must tell an Edina buyer in writing

Minnesota's seller disclosure law, Section 513.55, applies to Edina sales. You must disclose known material facts in good faith before signing the purchase agreement. Three topics have their own statutes.

  • Radon test history and mitigation, plus the state warning, under Section 144.496.
  • Wells, or a statement that you know of none, under Section 103I.235.
  • Whether sewage goes to a permitted treatment facility, under Section 115.55.

If you have radon test reports, mitigation receipts or well records, attach them to the disclosure so the buyer sees the same documents you do.

Can I turn my Edina house into a rental or an Airbnb?

As a long-term rental, yes, with a license. As a short-term rental, no. VRBO and Airbnb are not allowed in Edina, and a single-family house that is not owner-occupied may be occupied by a tenant only for 30 consecutive days or more.

The rental program requires an annual license for any dwelling that is not owner-occupied. Fees are $206 for a single unit such as a house, townhome or condo, $412 for a duplex with both sides rented, and $206 plus $17 per unit for apartments. Single-family and condo rentals are inspected every other year. Edina Public Health handles licenses at 952-826-0370.

If a buyer asks about boundary markers, remember that corner irons can be moved during utility or street work, and that fences, hedges and sidewalk edges are not reliable indicators of lot lines. Call Gopher State One Call at 651-252-1166 before anyone digs to locate the iron.

Hennepin County bills Edina property tax, due May 15 and October 15, or the next business day when either date lands on a weekend or holiday. Tax staff can be reached at 612-348-3011. Penalties for late payment come from Minnesota Statutes 279.01.

When the deed is recorded, Minnesota's deed tax is 0.33 percent of net consideration under Section 287.21. For a sale above $3,000 a Certificate of Real Estate Value goes to the county auditor under Section 272.115, and the assessor removes the seller's homestead classification for the following year unless the buyer qualifies for it. Ask your title company for the exact deed tax figure early.

Realistic ways to sell in Edina

  • Traditional listing: suited to a house in good order. Expect to prepare it, show it and wait for a buyer's financing.
  • For sale by owner: you set the price and handle the contract and disclosures yourself.
  • Cash sale as is: useful for an estate, a tenant-occupied house, or a home needing work the owner does not want to fund.

Whichever you choose, request written numbers and compare what you net after fees, repairs and carrying costs. With values this high, small differences in fees or repair budgets add up, so line the offers up side by side. Ask each buyer for a closing date and for the conditions in writing, and ask the title company which documents it will need from you, such as radon reports, well records and any rental license paperwork.

Is Edina a good place to sell quickly?

Values are high and the city is more than 95 percent developed. A house with deferred repairs, an estate sale or a tenant in place often moves faster through a direct cash purchase than through a repaired and staged listing.

Can I use my Edina house as a short-term rental while I sell?

No. Short-term rentals like VRBO and Airbnb are not allowed in Edina. A non-owner-occupied house can be rented, but only for stays of at least 30 consecutive days and with the annual rental license.

How much does an Edina rental license cost?

A single unit costs $206 per year and a duplex with both sides rented costs $412. Apartments cost $206 plus $17 per unit. The city bills separately after it processes your application.

Do I owe deed tax when I sell my Edina house?

Minnesota imposes the deed tax when the deed is presented for recording, at 0.33 percent of net consideration. Who pays it is set by your purchase agreement, so confirm with your title company before you sign.

Who do I call about Edina property taxes?

Call Hennepin County's property tax team at 612-348-3011. Taxes are due May 15 and October 15. Your closing statement will show how the current year's tax is split between you and the buyer.

Three ways to sell a Minnetonka house fast

A Minnetonka owner can list with an agent, sell privately, or accept cash from a buyer who takes the house as it stands. The cash route fits best when repairs are pending, tenants are in place, or the closing date cannot slide.

Every route runs through the same paperwork. The parcel is in Hennepin County, so the county bills the tax and files the deed. Minnetonka also keeps its own assessor, so a value question goes to city hall instead of the county offices downtown.

Minnetonka housing snapshot

Most Minnetonka households own, and values run high. About 28 percent of homes are rentals, and 88.2 percent of residents lived at the same address a year earlier, so turnover is modest. The 2025 population estimate is 53,969.

Three school districts cover the city: Hopkins in the central and eastern part, Minnetonka in the west, and Wayzata along the northern edge. Name the district in your listing description, since the answer shifts from one street to the next.

Rental registration rules

Minnetonka requires registration for every rental property, however short the stay. The ordinance was adopted on December 18, 2023 and took effect on February 3, 2024. Each certificate lapses one year after submission, and renewal notices arrive by email.

  • Condo and townhome owners name the unit being rented.
  • Single-family houses, duplexes and triplexes need one application per unit.
  • The designated property manager must be able to respond in person when something goes wrong.

The council passed a short-term rental ordinance on June 8, 2026. Stays under 30 days now require both a registration and a homestead, so only an occupant who treats the home as a primary residence may rent all or part of it. An investor reading your listing will weigh that limit. Request the ordinance text from the city before telling anyone that a short-term use is permitted.

What Minnesota requires a Minnetonka seller to put in writing

Residential sellers owe the buyer a written disclosure before any agreement is signed, as Minnesota Statutes section 513.55 directs. You must name each material fact you know of that would significantly and adversely affect how an ordinary buyer uses and enjoys the home. Write it honestly and from what you actually know. Handing it to the buyer's licensee counts as delivery, and the licensee can pass it on.

A few records make the form easier to complete.

  • Older building permits, which sit in the city's records archive.
  • The location of property stakes and buried utility lines, which residents can trace with a metal detector borrowed from the city.
  • Anything you know about water, drainage or foundation trouble near the creek or the lake shore.

New permit applications, payments and plan reviews all happen online. Phone 952-939-8394 to learn how long a review is running before an open permit delays your closing.

Hennepin County taxes and a Minnetonka sale

Tax bills split into two payments, May 15 and October 15. When a due date falls on a weekend or holiday, you get until the next business day. The next first-half date, May 15, 2027, is a Saturday, so the payment moves to Monday, May 17.

Questions about your value or classification go to the city assessor at 952-939-8220. The county fixes values as of January 2 and mails notices in March. April and May are the window for informal talks. A formal appeal begins at the local board. Next is the county board of appeal and equalization in mid-June, and Minnesota Tax Court is the other formal route.

  • E-check payments online carry no fee. Cards, PayPal and Venmo add a service charge.
  • A check sent by mail needs a postmark no later than the due date.
  • To pay in person, go to the Government Center at 300 South 6th Street, 6th floor, on a weekday. A drop box on that floor accepts checks through the early evening.
  • Lender escrow folds the taxes into the mortgage payment, so a new owner may never see the bill.

Three notices arrive each year. The valuation notice comes in March, the proposed levies notice in November, and the tax statement in March with payment stubs. The November estimate leaves out special assessments that may be added to the final bill, and it gives the dates of the truth-in-taxation meetings where residents can comment on budgets.

Removing a late-payment penalty

Hennepin County will erase a late-payment penalty one time in any ten years, and only on the current year's taxes. The application deadline is June 30 for a first-half payment and November 30 for a second-half payment, and the full tax must already be paid. Clear any older balance on the parcel before you set a closing date, because it blocks the request.

A step-by-step order for a quick Minnetonka sale

Begin with the paperwork you control: older permits from the city archive and a finished disclosure statement. For a rental, check that the registration is current and explain to the buyer what happens to the tenants. Next, collect cash offers and compare the closing date, the check amount and each closing line. Pick one, sign, and let the buyer order title work. At closing the deed goes to Hennepin County for recording, and any unpaid tax or special assessment is paid from the proceeds. Keep the tax statement and your last payment receipt handy so the title company sees what is owed and what is paid.

What to ask before taking a cash offer

Get the proposal on paper, showing the closing date, the check amount, and who covers each closing line. A company buying in present condition should say whether it plans any repairs, and you should be equally direct about what you know of the house.

  • Does the offer depend on an inspection or on financing?
  • Who orders the title search, and who pays recording charges?
  • If tenants live there, what becomes of their lease?
  • May you stay a couple of weeks after closing to finish moving?

A quick sale still needs the disclosure statement, a deed and a trip to the county recorder. What it removes is months of showings. Set the cash figure beside what a listing would net after repairs, commissions, and the months of mortgage, insurance and utilities you would carry. Then pick the route that matches your calendar.

Does a Minnetonka landlord need to keep the registration active during a sale?

Yes, while tenants live there. The city registers every rental regardless of length, and a certificate lasts one year. Renew before the expiration printed on it.

Who sets my Minnetonka house's value for tax purposes?

The city assessor, reachable at 952-939-8220, and not the county office. Hennepin County still collects the money and holds the county appeal board in mid-June.

When does the next Hennepin County tax payment come due?

The first half is due May 15, 2027. That is a Saturday, which moves the deadline to Monday, May 17, and the second half follows on October 15.

Can my buyer run short-term rentals out of the house?

Only as an owner living there. The June 8, 2026 ordinance requires a homestead and a city registration for any stay under 30 days.

Can a late tax penalty be removed in Hennepin County?

Sometimes. The county allows one abatement every ten years, for current-year taxes. The second-half deadline is November 30, and you must first pay the tax in full, with nothing left over from earlier years.

What is different about selling in St. Louis Park

St. Louis Park requires a city housing inspection whenever a property is sold or ownership is transferred. That step comes before closing, so it shapes how fast any sale can go, whether you list the house or take a cash offer.

  • Listing: the seller arranges the inspection, and corrections are usually made before the closing.
  • Direct sale: the same inspection applies, so book it early.
  • Cash offer: a buyer can take the house with open corrections through the city's escrow option, described below.

The city and its homes

St. Louis Park is a first-ring suburb just west of Minneapolis, next to Edina, Golden Valley, Minnetonka, Plymouth and Hopkins. The July 2025 population estimate is 50,027, nearly the same as the 50,010 counted in 2020. Interstate 394, U.S. Highway 169 and State Highways 7 and 100 run through it, and the public schools are Independent School District 283.

Most houses here date from one building boom. The city grew from 7,737 people in 1940 to 22,644 in 1950 and 43,310 in 1960, and about 60 percent of its homes went up between the late 1940s and early 1950s. The inspector reads each house against the code in place when it was built, so roofs, siding, garages and interiors are the four areas to walk first.

How the sale inspection works

A city inspector visits for about 45 to 60 minutes to check that the siding, roof, garage and interior meet the property maintenance code. Appointments are usually available within one to three days.

The fee covers the first inspection and any follow-ups: $360 for a single-family house or townhouse, $460 for a duplex and $250 for a condominium. With no violations, the city issues a property maintenance certificate. It lasts one year for a house, townhouse or duplex and two years for a condo.

If violations turn up, the city issues a correction notice. In most cases repairs must meet the code in force when the building was built, and remodeled areas follow the code from the year of the remodel. Smoke detectors are the exception and are required in every building.

Temporary certificate and escrow

If repairs can't be finished before closing, the buyer can take a temporary property maintenance certificate by signing an escrow agreement and finishing the work within 90 days of closing.

  • Seller repairs: the usual path, followed by a return visit to verify the work.
  • Cost and timing: the escrow agreement costs $155, must be prepared 48 hours before closing, and needs enough money held in escrow to cover the listed work.
  • Before the visit: the city publishes a list of commonly noted property maintenance deficiencies as a PDF.
  • Permits: all open permits must be closed before an escrow agreement can be approved.
  • Questions: the city's escrow line is 952.924.2588.

Home values and household size

A typical owner's home is valued at $386,800 for 2020 to 2024, and occupants own 57.8 percent of homes. The average household is small, at 1.99 people.

Rental licensing and a sale

The city requires an annual business license before a tenant moves into a single-family home, duplex, townhome or condo that the owner does not occupy. Rental licenses cover non-owner-occupied units, including single-family homes, townhomes, condominiums and multifamily buildings.

The requirement does not apply to a dwelling the owner occupies for at least six months per calendar year, or to rooms rented inside an owner-occupied home. A seller renting a house should confirm the license is current, since a buyer who keeps the tenant will inherit that duty. The city also offers rental license ordinance training for owners.

A rented house still needs the sale inspection at transfer. Ask the city's Housing office whether anything else is due at transfer before you set a closing date.

Hennepin County taxes and assessing

Hennepin County bills property tax in two halves, due May 15 and October 15, or the next business day when either falls on a weekend or holiday. Late payments carry penalties that grow each month, and a late payment is applied to penalty first and then to tax.

St. Louis Park runs its own assessing office, so valuation notices come from the city and not the county. Call 952-924-2535. Notices go out in March, informal discussion happens in April and May, and the county board of appeal and equalization meets in mid-June.

Hennepin accepts e-checks online with no fee, up to $50,000 per transaction, and card, PayPal or Venmo payments with a service fee. Many owners instead pay through a mortgage escrow account, in which case the lender receives the payment information, so ask the servicer for the payoff before closing.

  • Penalty abatement: an owner may ask once every ten years, with applications due June 30 for the first half and November 30 for the second.
  • Delinquency: taxes unpaid by January 1 of the next year become delinquent, with a one-year or three-year redemption period by property class.
  • Questions: Hennepin property tax staff are at 612-348-3011 on weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and they reply to email within about one business day.

Order of steps for a quick sale

Book the city inspection first, since it gates everything else. While you wait for the appointment, walk the roof, siding, garage and interior yourself and fix what you can. Ask the servicer or the county for the payoff on both tax halves, and close any open permits. If the house is a rental, confirm the license is current.

A listing adds showings, a buyer's loan and an appraisal on top of the inspection. A cash sale skips the loan and appraisal, and the escrow option lets the buyer take on open corrections after closing. That leaves the inspection, title work and permits as the main timing items either way. Tell the buyer up front what the inspector flagged and what you fixed, and keep the certificate or the escrow agreement with your closing papers. A buyer who sees a clean certificate has less reason to ask for a lower price, and a cash buyer can weigh open corrections against an offer without waiting for a second visit.

Do I need an inspection to sell my house in St. Louis Park?

Yes. The city requires a housing inspection whenever a property is sold or ownership transfers. The fee is $360 for a single-family house or townhouse, $460 for a duplex and $250 for a condo.

How long is the St. Louis Park property maintenance certificate good for?

It lasts one year for single-family homes, townhomes and duplexes, and two years for condominiums. It is issued once an inspector finds no code violations or confirms repairs are complete.

Can the buyer finish the repairs after closing in St. Louis Park?

Yes, through a temporary property maintenance certificate. The buyer signs an escrow agreement, funds the cost of the work, pays a $155 fee, and completes everything within 90 days of closing. Call 952.924.2588 with questions.

When are Hennepin County property taxes due for a St. Louis Park house?

They are due May 15 and October 15. When either date falls on a weekend or holiday, the due date moves to the next business day.

Who assesses property in St. Louis Park?

The city's own assessing office handles valuation notices, at 952-924-2535. Hennepin County handles tax billing and collection, so keep both offices in your contact list.

Selling quickly in Shakopee

You can list with an agent, sell on your own, or accept cash from a buyer with no lender involved. Speed comes down to the shape of the house, whether the title is clean, and how quickly you can gather the Scott County paperwork.

  • Agent listing: fits a house that is ready to move into, if you can wait out showings and the buyer's loan.
  • Private sale: no agent fee, but you handle the price, the disclosures and the purchase agreement.
  • Cash offer: a match for repairs, unpaid taxes, inherited title or renters, because the buyer accepts the house in its current state.

Even a house needing a roof, a tenant move-out or an estate clean-out can sell here. The problem simply points toward one route over another.

Shakopee at a glance

Shakopee is where Scott County keeps its government, set along the Minnesota River southwest of Minneapolis. Its growth spurt began when U.S. Highway 169 was rerouted to the Bloomington Ferry Bridge in 1996. The city had 20,568 people in 2000 and 37,076 in 2010, then 43,698 in April 2020. The estimate for July 2025 is 49,366, roughly 5,700 more residents than five years earlier.

County Highway 101 crosses the historic downtown from east to west, while Highway 169 and State Highway 13 link the city to the metro. Buyers know the area for Valleyfair, Canterbury Park and the Landing, a historic village on the river. Public schooling is Independent School District 720, with Shakopee High School and two middle schools. The city covers 28.44 square miles.

Home values and rent

A typical owner-occupied home here is valued at $374,800, and owners live in 74.8 percent of homes. Median gross rent runs $1,531 a month. Use the median only as a rough marker, because a house needing repairs will land under it.

Rental rules that affect a sale

City rules reach a rented house. All rentals, including single-family homes, have to be registered on the Shakopee ePortal, and a tenant in the house brings that record into the sale.

The city's R-HOME program asks owners to complete Phase I landlord training within a year of getting a rental certificate. Buildings of four or more units need Phases I, II and III. Tenant background checks come before move-in. If the buyer wants the tenant to stay, expect a question about whether the certificate and training are up to date.

  • Registration: file it online through the city ePortal.
  • Training: the Phase I certificate is accepted by other cities, and the city usually hosts a session in spring.
  • Fair housing: the City Council approved a Fair Housing Policy in May 2019, and complaints go to the Minnesota Department of Human Rights, since the city doesn't take them in.

Questions about fair housing duties during a sale can go to the Department of Planning and Development at 952-233-9300. Find out early whether the buyer wants the tenant to stay, since that determines if the contract needs a move-out date.

How Scott County values and taxes a Shakopee house

Taxes start with the value the Scott County assessor assigns. By state law, 20 percent of all property is inspected in person every year, which puts your neighborhood on a roughly five-year cycle. Notices of value arrive around March.

Owners can refuse an interior inspection, in which case the assessor guesses at the interior and the local board of review won't reduce your value until you allow one. Values can move by any amount now that the old 15 percent limit program ended with taxes payable in 2010.

  • First half: due May 15, payable by mail, drop box, online, or at the Government Center at 200 4th Avenue West in Shakopee.
  • Second half: due October 15.
  • Homestead and disability relief: the county accepts residential homestead applications and helps eligible honorably discharged service members with service-connected disabilities claim the state's market value exclusion. See whether either applies to your parcel.
  • Appeals: Minnesota Tax Court filings are due April 30 of the year the taxes are payable.
  • Mailing: postmarks now show when the Postal Service first handles an envelope, so pay online or request a hand postmark.

Before you close

Begin on the county's property information site. A parcel page there lists the legal description, tax detail, valuation, recorded documents and certificate of real estate value. Search by house number plus the first few letters of the street name.

Because the data refreshes weekly, phone Property and Taxation Services at 952-496-8115 for an exact payoff. That is most important when the parcel is under a confession of judgment contract for past-due years.

  • Make sure the owner on record is the same person signing the deed.
  • Get the balance on both halves from the county, special assessments included.
  • For a former rental, collect the registration and the training certificate.
  • When an heir is selling, ask the county recorder what has to be filed before a deed can be recorded.
Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Shakopee houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Closing day and what a cash sale skips

The closing agent normally orders these searches, yet a seller with answers in hand loses less time. A listing typically runs offer, loan approval, appraisal, closing. A cash purchase drops the lender and appraisal, so the buyer's title company can set a closing date as soon as the owner, tax balance and liens check out.

Unpaid taxes get paid out of the sale proceeds at closing, so ask the county for the figure a few days ahead. An inherited house usually stalls on the open estate, which is why the recorder question deserves an early answer.

Bring photo ID for every owner who signs, and keep the latest tax statement, any rental registration and training certificate, and the notice of value together in one folder. If you are working with a cash buyer, those same papers let the title company check the owner, the balance owed and the recorded documents without repeated requests to you. Ask the county for anything that looks stale before the closing date is set, not the week of closing.

Frequently asked questions

Is a cash offer faster than listing a house in Shakopee?

Often, since nobody waits on a buyer's loan or a lender's appraisal. Title work still sets the pace, and a clean title closes faster than one with liens or an open estate.

Do I have to let the Scott County assessor inside my house?

No, you can refuse, and the assessor will estimate the interior. The tradeoff is that the local board of review won't lower your value until you allow an inspection.

When are Shakopee property taxes due?

May 15 for the first half and October 15 for the second. Near a deadline, pay online or request a manual postmark, since mail postmarks now reflect the day the Postal Service first processes it.

Do I need rental registration to sell a rented house in Shakopee?

Yes, every rental in the city, single-family houses too, is registered through the ePortal. Owners also finish R-HOME Phase I training within a year of a certificate, so keep those records for the buyer.

Where do I find out what I still owe on a Shakopee parcel?

Search the Scott County property information site, then call Property and Taxation Services at 952-496-8115 for today's number. Online data updates weekly, so a quick call before closing is wise.

Selling a Moorhead house on a short timeline

If you need out quickly, you can hire an agent, market the house yourself, or take cash from a buyer who accepts it as is. Cash fits best when repairs have piled up, a tenant lives there, or a job or family change sets your move date.

Each path ends at the Clay County Recorder, and a rental adds one stop at city hall. The sections below cover the Moorhead and Clay County rules that most often decide how fast a closing can go.

Moorhead housing snapshot

Moorhead is the Clay County seat, on the Red River directly across from Fargo, North Dakota. The city has added residents quickly since 2020, and renters occupy a large share of its homes. Because so many houses are rentals, the city's rental rules come up in a good share of sales.

Renters occupy 41.9 percent of homes, and about 80 percent of residents had not moved in the past year.

Rental registration before a sale

If anyone but you or a relative lives in the house, registration is required. Moorhead covers single-family homes, multiplexes, condos, mobile homes and rooming arrangements, and it also reaches an owner-occupied house with a room rented to an unrelated person. A house where your child's own family lives does not need it if you live elsewhere. Accepting anything in exchange for housing, even groceries or maintenance work, counts as rent.

  • Registration renews every year, with the renewal due December 31.
  • Inspections are done annually, though a high scorer may self-inspect the next year.
  • A new owner must call Neighborhood Services at 218-299-5434 and file the application before taking possession.
  • The city will not register a unit unless the owner is current on property taxes and other obligations to the city.

A buyer who wants to convert a single-family house into a rental can pay $100 for a pre-purchase inspection. If the house is currently a rental, tell your buyer up front so the registration and renewal fee are settled before the closing date.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Moorhead house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Taxable value and homestead status

The city assessor sets market value as of January 2 each year, and Clay County collects the taxes. The assessor must view every property at least once every five years, and a building permit can trigger a visit.

Homestead status lowers the taxable value for an owner who lives in the house. Under the city's formula the exclusion is 40 percent of the first $95,000 of value, capped at $38,000, and it shrinks by 9 percent of the value above $95,000. A buyer applies in their own name. December 31 is the date to occupy the home and file for the next assessment year.

How to appeal your assessment

  • Valuation notices come with the tax statement in late March or early April.
  • The local board of appeal and equalization hears formal appeals in mid-April, on the date printed on the notice.
  • The county board meets in mid-June, and you must have appealed locally first.
  • Most real estate pays half of its tax on May 15 and the rest on October 15.

Call the assessor's office at 218-299-5310 with questions about a specific parcel. Many questions end there, after a look at comparable sales or a correction to the property details on file.

What the Clay County Recorder needs to record a Moorhead deed

The Recorder's office, at the Government Center on 12th Avenue South in Moorhead, publishes a checklist for deeds. Missing one item can send a package back. When several documents share a single check and any one is not in recordable form, the office returns all of them unrecorded and does not issue refunds.

  • The recording fee, which is $46, and the title of the document on the first page.
  • A Certificate of Real Estate Value filed online when the price is over $3,000, with a $54 well certificate that goes with it.
  • The state deed tax, a complete legal description rather than the shortened version on a tax statement, and a tax statement mailing address.
  • A drafted-by statement and a full acknowledgment, with the notary's seal, signature and commission expiration.
  • Delinquent real estate taxes paid first, through the County Auditor at 218-299-5006.
  • A septic certificate for rural residential property, which does not delay recording.

Records can be viewed at 3510 12th Avenue South on weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and the land records site is searchable around the clock. Write one check to Clay County for the fees and deed tax, and use a separate check for any delinquent taxes. Splitting a tax parcel requires current taxes in full and may need a survey. The Recorder cannot give legal advice or pick a form for you.

What to check before closing on a cash offer

Ask when the buyer wants possession, then confirm each of these points in writing.

  • Who pays the rental registration renewal if a rental closes late in the year.
  • Who handles the well and septic paperwork, if the property has either.
  • How the buyer will treat the tenant's current lease and deposit.
  • The date money reaches you, and how any delinquent tax or special assessment is paid out of the proceeds.

The city's property information site shows special assessment history, permit records, sales history and valuations. Print what it shows before you talk numbers with a buyer.

A simple order of steps

Sort the tax and registration questions first, since both can stall a closing. Pay any delinquent tax through the County Auditor. If the house is a rental, settle the registration with Neighborhood Services. Then gather the legal description and the tax statement mailing address, choose your buyer, and agree on a possession date. On closing day, one check covers the recording fee and deed tax, and a separate check covers any delinquent tax. Keep your notary's seal and commission details in view when the deed is signed, because an incomplete acknowledgment sends the whole package back.

Frequently asked questions

Does a family member living in my Moorhead house make it a registered rental?

No, not when the owner lives elsewhere and the occupants are related to the owner. Registration is required when unrelated people live there, including college roommates, or when you take anything in exchange for housing.

Where do I take a question about my Moorhead assessed value?

Call the Moorhead Assessor's Office at 218-299-5310. The city only keeps values for parcels inside city limits, so a property outside the limits goes to the Clay County Assessor.

What will Clay County charge when my deed is recorded?

The recording fee is $46, plus the state deed tax of 0.33 percent of the price when it exceeds $3,000. A $54 well certificate is also due when a Certificate of Real Estate Value is required.

What is the cutoff for homestead status on a Moorhead house?

December 31 is the deadline to occupy the home and file the application for the current assessment year. Taxes on that assessment are payable the following year, and a new buyer applies in their own name.

Can I skip the local board and appeal straight to the Clay County board?

No. You must first appeal to the local board in April to earn the right to go to the county board in June. Call the assessor early, because many questions are settled with comparable sales or corrected property details.

Which sale route moves fastest in Mankato?

Three routes are open: an agent, a sale on your own, or a cash offer. Which one fits depends on what you own: a rental, a student-area property or a family home. Mankato is the Blue Earth County seat, and its 2025 population of 46,529 is 4.4 percent above the 2020 base.

Half of Mankato's homes are owner-occupied, and renters typically pay $1,132 a month. Because so many houses are rented, the buyer pool includes first-time owners and people who want another rental. Minnesota State University, Mankato keeps student demand alive in parts of town. A tired rental or an empty house can sell faster to a cash buyer than to someone waiting on a mortgage and an appraisal.

  • Agent listing: widest exposure to buyers, but the slowest path to closing.
  • Investor purchase: hardly any showings, and the closing date is yours to name.
  • Sale by owner: you deal with buyers, the written disclosure and all the forms yourself.

Mankato housing numbers

Mankato has a short commute and a lower price point than the Twin Cities. A typical owner-occupied home is valued at $261,700. The city counts 18,075 households, owners with a mortgage pay a median $1,624 monthly, and the drive to work averages 13.9 minutes.

Which county taxes and records your Mankato house?

Mankato lies in three counties. The city extends into Blue Earth, Nicollet and Le Sueur counties. Most addresses fall in Blue Earth, but your tax statement and deed name the county that applies to your parcel, so check them before you list.

Recording matters here. Minnesota Statutes 507.34 puts an unrecorded deed behind any later good-faith buyer who records first, which is why closing agents file at once.

The state deed tax under section 287.21 takes 0.33 percent of net consideration on prices over $3,000, paid when the deed reaches the recorder. The purchase agreement says who pays.

Rental licenses and zoning

In Mankato a rental license depends on the zoning of the lot, a point that counts for any house once used or planned as a rental. Low-density districts R-1 and R-2 limit occupancy to two unrelated people or a family, while R-3, R-4 and office-residential districts allow five unrelated people or a family.

  • Parking: two off-street stalls per unit in R-1 and R-2, paved with asphalt or concrete, each at least 8 by 18 feet.
  • Units: R-2 can license up to two units depending on lot size, and R-3 up to eight.
  • Grandfathered licenses: an existing license keeps its status only until it lapses, and then a new application meets current code.

A new rental application goes to the Intergovernmental Center, 10 Civic Center Plaza, with payment, a site plan and floor plans drawn to scale. If off-street parking cannot be met, no license is issued and no further inspections happen. Holding a license now? Get the city to say in writing whether it is grandfathered and active. Once a license lapses, the next owner applies under current code, and that can change what the house is worth to a landlord.

Blue Earth County property taxes

Blue Earth County bills over 31,000 parcels. When a due date lands on a weekend or holiday, it moves to the next business day. Statements are mailed by March 31 and are based on the previous year's valuation.

Blue Earth County property tax due dates
Property typeFirst halfSecond half
Most real estateMay 15October 15
Agricultural landMay 15November 15
Manufactured homesAugust 31November 15

Each valuation is set as of January 2. An appraiser visits every property about once in five years, with added visits for new building and improvements. State guidance keeps the county's overall assessment level between 90 percent and 105 percent of market value.

Online, you can look up a parcel by address or number to see current and past tax, special assessments and each taxing body's share, and pay electronically. Escrow through your lender does not end your duty to confirm the bill was paid, and you still get a statement.

How to appeal your valuation

Think the value is wrong? Start with a call to the assessor at (507) 304-4251. A formal petition goes to the Minnesota Tax Court by April 30 of the year the tax is payable, with service on the county by email or in person at 410 South 5th Street.

Winter and school questions from buyers

Winters hit hard at the meeting of the Minnesota and Blue Earth rivers. Snow cover lasts into March, so insulation, furnace condition and a sound roof are visible concerns. Mankato Area Public Schools serve Mankato, North Mankato, Eagle Lake and Madison Lake, with Mankato West and Mankato East high schools.

Buyers who commute use U.S. Highways 14 and 169 or Minnesota Highways 22 and 60, and local buses run through the Mankato Transit System.

Selling a student-area rental

Has the house sheltered students? Round up the lease, the license and any inspection results first. Compare the number of people living there with the zoning limit, because a rental buyer will do the same math. Timing matters too: leases tied to the school year can limit showings, and a vacant house is easier to show and to close on. If the house is vacant and tired, a cash buyer can take it as it stands and skip the repairs a lender would require.

Why the county line matters to timing

A parcel in Nicollet or Le Sueur County means different offices, phone numbers and forms than one in Blue Earth. Learn which courthouse holds your file before you promise a buyer a date. A few minutes with the parcel number saves a week of forwarded calls, and a buyer working with a deadline will appreciate that you already know who to contact.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

What happens at closing

A title company checks the record, drafts the deed and sends it to the recorder at once. Closing day means signing, giving up the keys, and getting paid after the mortgage and any taxes are cleared. A few days ahead, confirm the county and parcel number from your statement and request a payoff figure if you owe anything.

Who is a cash buyer a good fit for?

A cash sale can help a landlord getting out, an heir managing an estate from far away, or an owner whose neglected repairs would worry an appraiser. Because Mankato rental licenses turn on zoning, parking and a housing inspection, a cash buyer can weigh those factors without waiting for a mortgage commitment.

Get the offer in writing with the closing date, how closing costs split and proof of funds. Then put it next to what a listing would leave you after repairs and the months of carrying costs, and add anything you would owe the county.

Frequently asked questions

Is Mankato in Blue Earth County?

Mostly. It is the county seat, but part of the city lies in Nicollet and Le Sueur counties, and your tax statement names the one that bills your parcel.

What are the Blue Earth County tax payment dates?

Most real estate pays on May 15 and October 15. Agricultural land pays the second half on November 15 instead.

How many unrelated people can rent a Mankato house in R-1 or R-2 zoning?

Two. Low-density districts limit occupancy to two unrelated individuals or a family, and the unit needs two paved off-street parking stalls.

What does the state charge on the deed for a Mankato sale?

Sales above $3,000 owe 0.33 percent of the net amount, due when the deed is recorded. The purchase agreement sets who pays.

Can I appeal my Mankato property value?

Yes. Begin with the Blue Earth County assessor, (507) 304-4251. If that fails, a petition on last year's value goes to the Minnesota Tax Court by April 30 of the year the taxes are payable.

Cottage Grove, in Washington County, lies roughly 10 miles south of Saint Paul beside the Mississippi. Cottage Grove is on the agency's list of communities where private wells are sampled. Permits and city rules

Cottage Grove takes permit applications online, and the Building Division at 651-458-2804 handles inspections and permits.   • The Code Enforcement Officer handles property maintenance concerns and runs the city's rental licensing program, so an owner with tenants should call the Building Division before a sale.

Close out any open permits before listing so a buyer's lender or inspector has nothing to question late in the deal.

City utility bills at closing

Title and closing companies request a utility estimate from the city, and the final amount is collected at the closing table. The city runs an online form for this, the Utility Billing Request for Real Estate Closing, and it covers both current and outstanding city utility bills.

Tell your closing agent early so the request goes in before the closing date.
