Which school district serves Chaska?

All of Chaska is in Eastern Carver County Schools, Independent School District 112, so the district name in a listing does not change from street to street. Elementary schools in the city include Clover Ridge, Jonathan and La Academia Spanish Immersion. The district's middle schools are Chaska Middle School East, Chaska Middle School West and Pioneer Ridge Middle School, and Chaska High School is the city's high school.

Southwest Christian High School is a private option, as are church-affiliated grade schools such as St. John's Lutheran and Guardian Angels Catholic School.

Rental home requirements

Every rental dwelling in Chaska must be registered with the city and pass an initial inspection, a program run by the Chaska Fire Department's Bureau of Fire Prevention. Annual renewal is due in January, and inspections repeat every two years after the first. Owners, managers and tenants can book one at 952-227-7458 during the posted Monday, Wednesday and Thursday windows.

Inspectors check wiring and safety items that a seller can fix before a sale:

  • Extension cords may power portable appliances only, and multi-plug adapters or daisy-chained power strips are prohibited.
  • Smoke alarms must work, and a carbon monoxide alarm must be within 10 feet of each sleeping room.
  • Steps with three or more risers need handrails, and porches more than 30 inches above grade need guardrails.
  • Each unit needs a fire extinguisher rated 1-A:10:B:C or better, and bedrooms need egress windows.

The city also grants transient accommodation licenses, and those can carry conditions such as an occupancy certificate and payment of outstanding utility bills. Ask city licensing staff before planning short stays.

Building permits in Chaska

Chaska's Building Inspections Department enforces the state building code. Permits that need no plan review, such as roofing, siding, window and door replacement, plumbing, mechanical and fireplace work, are filed online through the SmartGov portal. Permits that need plan review go by email as PDFs to inspections@chaskamn.gov, and inspections are scheduled at 952-448-9395. The counter at One City Hall Plaza is open 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on weekdays.

If you replaced a roof or windows recently, keep the permit and the final inspection record. A buyer's inspector or title agent may ask to see them.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Chaska houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How a Chaska deed is recorded

Deeds go to Carver County Land Records and Vitals at 600 East 4th Street in Chaska, open Monday to Friday, 8:00 to 4:30. The phone is 952-361-1930. Minnesota deed tax is 0.33% of net consideration under section 287.21, collected when the deed is presented.

The county also collects a $5 agricultural conservation fee and requires a certificate of real estate value for sales over $3,000, well information, and the sewage treatment disclosure on every transfer. Property tax questions go to 952-361-1910, and assessment and homestead questions go to 952-361-1960.

Selling a Chaska house with tenants or in an estate

Tenants and estates are the two situations where a lender-free sale helps most. With tenants in place, a buyer who plans to keep them will want the rental registration, the most recent inspection and the lease terms. A buyer who wants the house empty will build the time that takes into the price and the schedule.

With an estate, the paperwork about who may sign comes first. Sort that out with the title company and, if needed, an attorney before you advertise anything. Once authority is clear, the sale itself works like any other: a price, a title search, a signed deed and a recording at the county.

What to gather before you accept an offer

Start with the permit records for roofing, windows and mechanical work, then the latest rental inspection report if tenants have lived there. Add the well and sewage statements and your tax statement. If the home is in a manufactured home park, ask the park operator what its resale rules require before you set a closing date.

Offers differ in more than price. Cash buyers can often promise a closing within a few weeks, while a financed buyer's timeline rides on the lender. Have every buyer put the date and any conditions on paper so the offers can be lined up evenly.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Can I sell a Chaska manufactured home quickly?

Yes, but the buyer pool differs from detached houses, and park rules and financing can slow a conventional sale. Ask the park operator what its resale rules require before you set a closing date.

Does Chaska inspect rentals before I sell a landlord property?

Yes. Rentals pass an initial inspection and are reinspected every two years, with renewal due each January. Have the latest inspection report ready for any buyer who will keep tenants.

Which county handles recording for a Chaska house?

Carver County. Land Records and Vitals at 600 East 4th Street, Chaska, takes the deed, deed tax, conservation fee, certificate of real estate value and disclosures.

Are there Chaska permits I should check before listing?

Look for roofing, siding, window, plumbing, mechanical and fireplace permits, which Chaska files through its online portal. Call 952-448-9395 if you need to confirm an inspection was closed.

What is the Minnesota deed tax on a Chaska sale?

It is 0.33% of the net consideration, due when the deed is presented for recording. The title company will show the exact figure on your closing statement.

Selling in Ramsey?
We buy Ramsey houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

The fastest way to sell a house in Ramsey

The fastest route is a direct sale to a buyer who accepts the house in its present state, because it skips showings, repair negotiations and a lender's appraisal. A listing with an agent takes longer but reaches the widest group of buyers, and a sale you run yourself sits between the two.

  • Direct sale: no repairs asked of you, a closing date you set, and a price that reflects the work.
  • Agent listing: more exposure, plus preparation, showings and the buyer's financing timeline.
  • Selling alone: you save the commission and handle every form and negotiation yourself.

Ramsey is an Anoka County suburb about 22 miles north-northwest of downtown Minneapolis. Many houses are not on city sewer, and about 4,200 private septic systems operate within its limits. That matters at sale time, as the next sections explain.

Ramsey housing snapshot

Ramsey is growing and family-heavy. It had 29,624 residents in mid-2025, a rise of 7.2% over the April 2020 base of 27,636, and 27,646 people were counted in 2020. About 85% of homes are lived in by their owners, and the typical household has 2.66 people.

Owners put the middle home's value at $359,600 for 2020 to 2024, while median gross rent is $1,826. Median household income is $116,415. About 92% of residents stayed in the same house for a full year. If your Ramsey house has a big lot, a finished lower level or a three-car garage, put those points first in your listing or your pitch to a direct buyer.

Septic inspection before you sell

If the house is on a private septic system, the city requires an inspection. Ramsey City Code section 113-23 calls for a compliance inspection on any sale or transfer of property served by an individual sewage treatment system. The city administers Minnesota Rules Chapter 7080.

  • An MPCA-certified inspector must perform the inspection and report on the state's approved form. City inspectors cannot do it.
  • You give the buyer a Certificate of Compliance at or before closing, and a copy of the inspection goes to the city's Building Division within 15 days.
  • If the sale falls between November 1 and April 30 and the inspection cannot be completed, the seller and buyer may agree in writing that it will be finished by the following June 1.
  • A system that fails normally has to be brought into compliance within 12 months.

Recent pumping does not replace the inspection, since pumping only addresses the tank and the inspector examines the entire system, including the drainfield. Each sale needs a new inspection even if you had one last year. Ask the Building Division at 763-433-9850 for the point-of-sale handout.

Owners of these systems also check for leaks and measure sludge and scum accumulations at least once every three years, and the city requires a septic pumping permit each time a tank is pumped. Keeping those permits and pumping records in a folder gives the inspector and the buyer a clear history of the system.

If your Ramsey house is a rental

Every residential rental in Ramsey needs a city license each year. Single-family rentals are inspected every three years, and multi-family buildings every year, against the 2021 International Property Maintenance Code, the city's rental code and its zoning code.

An inspection takes between 15 minutes and an hour. The inspector checks heating, plumbing and electrical systems, doors and windows, and exterior upkeep such as mowing, debris and vehicle licensing. A property that fails gets a correction list, and the license fee covers one follow-up visit. A third visit on the same issue can cost a $150 reinspection fee.

Two exceptions come up in sales. A house rented to a relative needs no license if it qualifies for Relative Homesteading with the Anoka County Assessor and you have applied for it. A contract for deed avoids licensing only if it is recorded with Anoka County and requires real principal payments, because an interest-only contract is treated as a rental. If you are selling with a tenant in place, give the buyer the latest inspection report and the license dates.

City utility accounts

A tenant may hold the account in a tenant's name, but the property owner stays responsible for any unpaid balance, and bills arrive quarterly. Bring the account current before closing, and call Utility Billing at 763-576-4343 if you need to add a second name or fix the billing address.

Anoka County recording charges

Anoka County's Land Records office records the deed. Its fee schedule, effective July 1, 2025, lists the following charges that apply to a typical sale.

Anoka County recording charges for a house sale
Recording chargeAmount
Recording fee for a deed (abstract)$46.00
Conservation fee$5.00
State deed taxNet consideration x 0.0033
Deed tax when consideration is $3,000 or less$1.65
Well certificate$54.00
Attested copy$2.00

The county also asks for a completed electronic certificate of real estate value, an eCRV number on the deed and a "send tax statements to" line naming the buyer. Any delinquent taxes have to be cleared before a transfer, and a split of a tax parcel requires current-year taxes to be paid. Instead of the $54 well certificate, a deed may carry the statement that the seller does not know of any wells on the property. Minnesota Statutes section 103I.235 sets that rule, and section 513.55 requires your written disclosure to the buyer before the purchase agreement is signed.

Steps for a quick Ramsey closing

Start with the septic inspection if the house has a system, since it has the longest lead time. Pump records and permits help the inspector. Next, settle the utility account and, for a rental, collect the latest inspection report and license dates. Pick your buyer and agree on a closing date in writing. The title company will clear any delinquent tax, prepare the deed with the eCRV number and the buyer's tax statement address, and record it with Anoka County. At closing you hand over the Certificate of Compliance and receive your proceeds after the deed tax and any unpaid balance are paid.

School districts

Two school districts serve the city, Elk River and Anoka-Hennepin, and PACT Charter School operates inside Ramsey. Confirm which district applies to your address before you print a school name in an advertisement.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need a septic inspection if I sell my Ramsey house in winter?

Yes, but the timing can shift. For sales between November 1 and April 30, the seller and buyer can close and agree that the inspection will be completed by the following June 1, if the inspection cannot be completed.

Who can perform a Ramsey point-of-sale septic inspection?

Only an MPCA-certified septic inspector. City inspectors do not perform these inspections, and the seller gives the buyer the Certificate of Compliance at or before closing.

Does a contract for deed make my Ramsey property a rental?

It can. If the contract is recorded with Anoka County and sets reasonable principal payments, the city does not require a rental license. An unrecorded or interest-only contract is treated as a rental.

What are the recording charges for a Ramsey deed?

Anoka County charges $46 to record a deed and $5 as a conservation fee, plus state deed tax of the net price times 0.0033. A well certificate costs $54 unless the deed carries the no-wells statement.

Who is responsible for the city utility bill when a Ramsey tenant lives there?

The owner. A tenant may hold the account, but the owner stays responsible for any unpaid balance, so settle it before closing. Call Utility Billing at 763-576-4343 to fix the billing address.

Selling in Prior Lake?
We buy Prior Lake houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

Ways to sell a Prior Lake house

A Prior Lake owner can go to market with an agent, handle the sale alone, or sell directly to a home-buying company. Which one makes sense usually comes down to condition, timing and whether the house sits on the water.

The city lies about 20 miles southwest of Minneapolis in Scott County, beside Savage and Shakopee, and State Highway 13 makes the commute easy. A well-kept house on a street near the lakes usually does fine on the open market. A house with a failing roof, an estate attached or a tenant who will not leave tends to suit a direct sale, where the buyer accepts the property in its present state and you pick the closing day.

  • Listing with an agent: broad reach, but you prepare the house and wait for a buyer's lender.
  • Selling it yourself: you keep the commission and take on the contract work.
  • Direct sale: little prep, a quick closing, and an offer that accounts for repairs.

Prior Lake owners and housing costs

Prior Lake is a family-and-owner city. About 86 of every 100 homes are lived in by the people who own them, and the typical household has 2.79 people. The estimated population reached 28,140 on July 1, 2025, up 1.9% from 27,616 in 2020.

Households earned a median of $134,255 over 2020 to 2024. Owners put the middle home's worth at $450,700, and renters paid a median of $1,654. Some 91% of residents were in the same home a year earlier, so most owners have been in place a while.

Short-term rental limits and your sale

Prior Lake permits only rentals of at least 60 days and no more than 180 days in its residential districts. Rentals shorter than 60 days are prohibited there, and a permit with a $250 application fee is required for the permitted range.

The rules live in City Code Sections 4-380 through 4-388. A permit expires each December 31 and cannot move to a new owner or a different dwelling, so a buyer of your house cannot inherit it. A named local agent who lives and works within 30 miles has to answer calls around the clock while the home is rented, and the dwelling must have off-street parking equal to the number of bedrooms. At most two restricted watercraft may be moored at the property. The ordinance caps overnight guests by lot size and floor area:

Overnight occupant limits for Prior Lake short-term rentals (City Code 4-384)
Lot sizeMain building under 1,500 sq ft1,500 to under 2,000 sq ft2,000 sq ft or more
One-half acre or more6812
Under one-half acre468

Children under three do not count toward these totals. A seller with a tenant under lease should pass along the lease and the permit file, and explain that the permit ends with the seller's ownership.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Prior Lake house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

City rules that can trip up a seller

The Code Enforcement Division enforces a long list of ordinances, and several of them come up while a house is being readied for the market. Fixing these items before a buyer's inspection saves you from last-minute credits.

  • Grass and weeds: growth taller than 12 inches is unlawful during the April 1 to November 1 growing season.
  • Snow on sidewalks: owners must clear public sidewalks within 48 hours after a snowfall ends.
  • Junk vehicles and debris: unlicensed or inoperable vehicles must be inside a building, and piles of boards or tires count as nuisances.
  • Recreational equipment: winter equipment may sit by the driveway from November 1 to April 1, and summer equipment from April to November 1, if it has current plates and runs.
  • Driveways and decks: replacing or widening a driveway takes a permit, and structures need a building permit.

Work near the shore carries lower limits. Moving more than 10 cubic yards of material, or disturbing more than 500 square feet, on steep slopes or in the bluff, shore impact or shoreland zones needs approval, while the threshold elsewhere is 50 cubic yards. A person who skips a required permit and applies afterward pays double the stated fee. Call Code Enforcement at 952-447-9811 before you start any project you plan to disclose or finish ahead of a sale.

Lakefront and lake-access homes

Prior Lake takes its name from two connected lakes, Lower Prior Lake at about 810 acres and Upper Prior Lake at about 354, linked by a navigable channel under Eagle Creek Avenue. Spring Lake, 290 acres, lies partly within the city along Scott County Road 12. The water is the reason many buyers look here.

Lakefront and lake-access homes are priced as a separate market from interior streets. Zebra mussels were confirmed in both the lower and the upper lake, so lake-property buyers sometimes ask about docks, lifts and invasive species. Have your dock and lift details ready, along with any permits you hold for shore work.

What Scott County requires when a house closes

Scott County's Land Records Department records deeds, mortgages, assignments, releases and satisfactions. It reviews each document for recordable form, but its staff cannot supply legal forms or advice, so use your title company or an attorney.

Under Minnesota Statutes section 513.55, you hand the buyer a signed statement of known defects ahead of the purchase agreement. Section 103I.235 adds a well statement on or with the deed. Sales above $3,000 also need a value certificate filed with the county, and the county and state websites list the deed tax rate and recording fees.

Scott County offers a free Property Watch alert that emails you whenever a document is recorded under your name and parcel number. Sign up before you sell if you want a record of when the deed lands.

A typical order of work: finish any permitted repairs, write the defect statement, check for wells, and let the title company file the value certificate and deed. Ask for the final settlement statement and compare it with your offer before you sign, and keep a copy of the recorded deed afterward.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Prior Lake houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Valuation and property tax

The county assessor values each parcel as of January 2 and mails a notice each March. Sales that are not arm's length, such as bank sales, short sales, foreclosures, auctions and transfers between relatives, are left out of its sales analysis. Appraisers walk about 11,000 parcels a year, so every property is viewed at least once every five years. The second half of the property tax is due October 15, so confirm it was paid before you close.

Frequently asked questions

Can I rent my Prior Lake house by the weekend?

No. Prior Lake prohibits rentals shorter than 60 days in every residential district. The city permits stays of 60 to 180 days with a permit and a $250 fee.

Does a short-term rental permit transfer to a buyer?

No. The permit cannot be transferred to another person or another dwelling, and it expires each December 31. A buyer who wants to rent the house must apply separately.

Which pre-sale fixes in Prior Lake need a city permit?

Building work, driveway replacement or widening, and some grading near the shore all need city permits. Starting without one means applying afterward at double the fee.

Where does a Prior Lake deed get recorded?

The Scott County Land Records Department does. Your title company normally handles the filing.

What is the sidewalk snow deadline in Prior Lake?

Forty-eight hours after the snowfall ends. Do not push snow into the street. Keep the walk clear while the house is listed, because showings continue all winter.

Elk River at a glance

Elk River is the Sherburne County seat, roughly 34 miles northwest of Minneapolis and 37 miles southeast of St. Cloud, where the Elk River meets the Mississippi. The city covers 42.33 square miles, so a house can sit in town, near the river or on a bigger lot toward the edge. Population is 27,896 as of July 2025, up 8.0 percent from the 25,840 counted in 2020.

The typical owner-occupied house is worth $370,100, and 79.2 percent of households own. Renters pay about $1,283 a month and household income is near $108,741. Owners with a mortgage spend a median $2,075 a month, and owners with no mortgage spend $796. If you are weighing a rental instead of a sale, that $1,283 rent is the number to compare against your own carrying costs.

  • U.S. 10 and U.S. 169 meet in the city and run together toward Anoka.
  • Minnesota Highway 101 connects to Interstate 94, about seven miles south.

Getting the house ready

Elk River winters are long, so buyers and inspectors look hard at the roof, attic insulation, furnace age and any history of ice dams or basement water. Gather your service records and receipts before the first showing, and keep a short list of any past leaks, repairs or replaced systems. A tidy folder answers questions quickly and helps whichever way you sell.

When you describe the house, name the school district. Elk River is in Independent School District 728, and parents often search by district number.

What Minnesota requires you to disclose

Before the purchase agreement is signed, you must disclose material facts you know about, under Section 513.55. Separate rules cover radon (144.496), wells (103I.235) and sewage (115.55, subdivision 6).

The sewage rule matters most if your property is not on city sewer. You must say whether sewage goes to a permitted facility. If it does not, the disclosure has to describe the system, include a map as far as practicable, note any abandoned system and attach any earlier inspection report. A seller who knew of a problem and stayed silent can be liable for the cost of bringing the system into compliance, and the buyer has two years to sue.

A certificate of compliance for an existing septic system is valid for three years, so a recent inspection can save you a step.

Rental licenses and permits in Elk River

The city requires a license for every rental dwelling, single-family houses included. Licenses are renewed and inspected each year. The rule that bites at a sale is Section 30-198 of the city code: a rental license cannot be transferred and ends automatically within 30 days after closing unless the new owner applies for and receives one.

A house rented on a platform like Airbnb needs a rental license when you are not on site with the guests. Renting a room does not need one if the owner and no more than two tenants share all living space. The Rental Dwelling Licensing Division is at 763-635-1075.

A shed over 200 square feet needs a permit, and permits lapse after 180 days without work or inspections. Residential permits that need plan review take about one to two weeks. Over-the-counter permits for roofing, siding or windows usually issue in one to two business days.

An owner who intends to sell needs a state contractor license when doing work on more than one property in a two-year period. Buyers can also look through the city's permit records, so finished work should have its permit on file.

Sherburne County taxes and recording

The county auditor-treasurer collects real estate tax in two halves, due May 15 and October 15, and the postmark decides penalty questions. Farm property pays in May and November instead. Call 763-765-4350 with questions.

The recorder's office is at 13880 Business Center Drive NW in Elk River, phone 763-765-4420. Recording a deed brings the state deed tax of 0.33 percent of net consideration (Section 287.21), plus a value certificate for any sale over $3,000 (Section 272.115). Your purchase agreement decides which side pays each.

If taxes are still owed when you sell, the title company normally pays them from your proceeds at closing. Ask the treasurer's office for a payoff figure ahead of time.

Selling a rental with open violations

An inspection failure does not stop a sale. Read the notice first and note the abate-by date. The city takes written extension requests before that date, and the licensing division can tell you what is still outstanding. Whoever buys the house gets the disclosure of the open items, so list them plainly. A buyer who plans to live in the house has no license to worry about, while one who plans to rent must apply within 30 days after closing.

Ways to sell an Elk River house

  • Agent listing: reaches the widest group of buyers, takes weeks, and may bring repair requests after the buyer's inspection.
  • Private sale: you handle pricing, showings, disclosures and the contract.
  • Cash sale as is: the buyer takes the property exactly as it stands today. That can suit a rental with a license problem, a house needing roof or furnace work, or an inherited property.

Ask each route for a written net-proceeds estimate so the comparison is fair. A cash sale skips showings, repair negotiations and a buyer's loan approval, and you pick the closing date within what the title work allows.

What to bring to a closing

Have photo ID, the keys and garage openers, and any rental license paperwork ready. If the house has a septic system or a well, bring the inspection reports and the well information. Closing is also when you hand over a recent tax statement and settle the final utility bills. The recorder files the deed afterward, usually through the title company.

What is the timeline for an Elk River sale?

Condition, price and financing drive it. A listing waits on showings and a buyer's loan, while a cash buyer can close as soon as title is ready. The Sherburne County recorder files the deed afterward.

What happens to my rental license when I sell in Elk River?

It ends. A rental dwelling license cannot be transferred and terminates within 30 days of closing unless the new owner applies for and is granted one. Report the sale to the Rental Dwelling Licensing Division at 763-635-1075.

Do I need to disclose my septic system?

If the property has one, yes. You must state in writing whether sewage goes to a permitted facility and, for a private system, describe it, show where it is and attach any earlier inspection report.

When are Sherburne County property taxes due?

Real estate pays in two halves, on May 15 and October 15, and farm property on May 15 and November 15. The county counts the postmark, so mail early. Call 763-765-4350 for payment options.

Can I sell an Elk River house that failed a rental inspection?

Yes, as is, with open violations disclosed to the buyer. The city accepts written extension requests before the abate-by date on a notice, and the licensing division at 763-635-1075 can list what is outstanding.

Your options for a fast Shoreview sale

There are three ways to sell: through an agent, to a buyer you find yourself, or for cash with no repairs required. The best fit turns on the work the house needs and your deadline.

  • Hire an agent if the house is clean and updated and several weeks of showings are fine.
  • Sell directly if a buyer is already lined up and you are comfortable writing the purchase agreement and disclosures.
  • Go with cash if the house needs work, is a rental or part of an estate, or has to close on a firm date.

Shoreview at a glance

Shoreview, in Ramsey County, is a second-ring suburb just north of Saint Paul. It has seven lakes, led by Turtle Lake, Snail Lake, Lake Owasso and Island Lake, and Drivers rely on Interstate 35W, Interstate 694 and County Highway 96. Land area is 10.77 square miles.

The city counted 25,043 people in 2010 and 26,921 in 2020. The July 2025 estimate, 26,906, is nearly identical, so the market is mostly existing houses changing hands.

The city is split between Mounds View (District 621) and Roseville (District 623), and which one a buyer gets depends on the side of the line the house is on. A listing should name the district that applies.

Housing and income figures

Owners live in 80.2 percent of Shoreview homes, about four in five, and the typical owner's home is valued at $383,700. The average commute is 22.2 minutes.

City permits before you sell

How much cleanup a sale needs often comes down to permits. Closing out an open or missing one now beats scrambling after a buyer's inspection turns it up.

  • Permits: roofing, siding, window, door, electrical, mechanical and plumbing jobs need one. Contractors apply online, and homeowners email permits@shoreviewmn.gov or go to City Hall.
  • Plan review: when a permit needs it, expect up to 10 working days.
  • Smaller jobs: fences, driveways, patios and sheds of 200 square feet or less are handled by Community Development, 651-490-4680.
  • Safety items: handouts cover decks, egress windows, finished basements, smoke alarms and carbon monoxide alarms.

If the lot is by a lake or slopes, ask Community Development about the erosion and sediment control handout, because grading standards are being updated. Overnight street parking is banned from 2 to 5 a.m. A permit covers up to seven days and five vehicles, handy during a move-out, though dumpsters and storage pods can't go on the street.

Rental licenses and selling a rental

Each rental property needs a license, which the city grants only when the unit meets city regulations and municipal utility bills and real estate taxes are paid in full. More than 600 rental locations are on the city's list.

There are three license types: a general dwelling license for a single-family home with an inspection every other year, a short-term rental license for stays of 30 days or less with an annual inspection and extra parking rules, and a multiple dwelling license for four or more units. Licenses expire December 31 and renew each year. The city began licensing short-term rentals and inspected over 300 rental homes in 2025.

When you sell a rented house, the city has a form to void the license once the property is sold. Settle that, and any unpaid utility bill, at the closing table so the next owner starts clean.

Ramsey County notices and records

Ramsey County sends two mailings each year. The first arrives in mid-March with the tax statement, showing both half-year amounts, and a notice of valuation and classification that sets next year's taxes. The second arrives in November, listing proposed taxes along with the levy and budget meeting dates.

Property Tax Services is at 90 Plato Boulevard West in Saint Paul, 651-266-2222. Deeds and mortgages are recorded with the Recorder and Registrar of Titles at 651-266-2050. Staff there can't help complete legal forms, and a recorded document is permanent, so have the deed reviewed before it goes in.

  • Ask Property Tax Services for the amount due on both halves of the current year.
  • Ask the Recorder which document types the sale needs, since fees and requirements differ by document.
  • For an estate sale, confirm who has authority to sign before scheduling the closing.
  • Read the November mailing: it previews next year's taxes and the budget meetings where residents can comment, which a buyer may ask about.

A practical order of steps

Start with the paper that can hold up a closing. Get the two half-year tax amounts from the county, check for open permits at City Hall, and, if the house is rented, line up the rental license and the form that voids it. Then decide how to sell. A listing adds showings, a buyer's mortgage and an appraisal. A cash sale skips those and leaves title work and the tenant's move-out date as the main timing issues.

For a rented house, settle the tenant's move-out date first, since a buyer who wants the house empty needs it in the contract. For an estate, confirm who can sign before any closing is scheduled. Either way, a seller with permits, taxes and licenses sorted tends to close sooner than one still chasing paper.

On closing day, the practical checklist is short. Bring photo ID for each owner who signs. Have the final utility readings and any unpaid city bill cleared so nothing follows the buyer. If the house was a rental, hand over the lease paperwork and let the city know the license is being voided. If the buyer is paying cash, the title company will usually run the same checks on taxes, liens and the owner of record, so the answers you gathered early are useful on either route, and they keep the closing date from slipping. Sellers who wait until the week of closing to call the county or the city usually find that one small item, such as a permit or a utility balance, needs several days to clear.

Frequently asked questions

How fast can a Shoreview house sell for cash?

A cash sale can close in a few weeks when the title is clear, since there is no lender underwriting to wait on. A lien, an unpaid utility bill or an unsettled estate can lengthen that. If the house is rented, settle the tenant's move-out date first.

Does Shoreview require a rental license for a single-family house?

Yes. A single-family rental needs a general dwelling rental license, which includes an inspection every other year, and the license renews each December 31. The city issues it only when utility bills and real estate taxes are paid in full.

What happens to a Shoreview rental license when I sell?

Use the city's form to void the license once the property has sold. Doing it promptly stops renewal notices and shows the city the unit changed hands.

When does Ramsey County mail property tax notices?

The tax statement and value notice go out in mid-March, and the proposed tax notice arrives in November. The statement shows the first and second half amounts for the year.

Is a permit needed to fix up a Shoreview house before listing?

Often yes. Roofing, siding, windows, doors, electrical, mechanical and plumbing work all need permits, and fences, driveways and small sheds go through Community Development. Call building inspections at 651-490-4683 to confirm before starting.

Timeline for an Austin sale

How quickly an Austin house sells comes down to the route and to how tidy the paperwork is. A cash buyer can close in a matter of weeks, while a listing runs on the buyer's lender and inspection calendar. Austin is the seat of Mower County in southeast Minnesota, so most of the paperwork runs through the Mower County offices on First Street NE.

You have three basic routes:

  • Sell on the open market and wait for financing and appraisal.
  • Sell privately to a neighbor, relative or investor and handle the paperwork yourself.
  • Accept a cash offer from a buyer who takes the house with every repair left to them.

Before any buyer walks through, you can shorten the timeline by sorting out four things: the permit history of the house, the property tax status, any city charges tied to the parcel, and whether the lot sits in an area that flooded in the past. The sections below cover each one.

Austin housing market

Austin has 26,689 residents, and buyers are mostly local workers, first-time purchasers and investors. A typical owner-occupied home is valued at $163,900, far below the figures in the Twin Cities suburbs. These are the numbers a seller is most likely to compare against an offer.

The same-house rate is 87.0 percent, so the market turns over slowly and a well-priced home stands out. At $953 a month, median rent is low as well, which is why some Austin owners keep a house as a rental and others decide to sell it. If you are weighing that choice, read the rental registration rules below first.

Flood history and your sale

A lot of Austin houses sit in the Cedar River floodplain, so buyers and lenders will raise it. The city's flood history lists major floods in July 1978, 1983, 1993, spring 2000 when the Cedar River crested at 23.4 feet, September 2004 and 2010. Dobbins Creek and Turtle Creek also run through town.

The city answered with buyouts. Flood-prone homes were purchased and demolished using a Community Development Block Grant and the Hazard Mitigation Grant Program, low areas were turned into parks, dikes were added after 2004, and a flood wall protecting downtown was finished in 2014. If your lot is near the river or one of the creeks, ask City Hall at 500 4th Avenue NE for the parcel's floodplain status before you list, and ask your insurance agent what flood coverage costs.

Tornadoes are the other weather risk on record. An EF2 tornado crossed the northwest and north side of Austin on June 17, 2009. Roof age, siding and tree condition are the details a buyer's inspector will notice.

Permits and yard rules

Check your permit record first. The city warns that if you sell a building with modifications done without a permit, you may be required to tear the addition down, leave it unoccupied or pay for costly repairs. Permits are usually needed for additions, decks, garages, fences, pools, water heaters, re-roofing and electrical, plumbing and heating work.

Two routine ordinances also generate liens against sellers who ignore them.

  • Grass and weeds. City Code 10.13 sets an 8 inch height limit. After a notice from the weed inspector you have seven days to comply, then the city cuts it and certifies the cost to the Mower County Auditor as a special assessment collected like real estate taxes.
  • Sidewalk snow. Chapter 7.04 requires owners to clear public sidewalks within 12 hours after snow stops, and the city may clear them after 24 hours and bill the owner.

Deal with both before closing. Austin also does not allow chickens, which matters if you kept hens and a buyer asks about the coop.

Rental registration when you sell

For a rental house, Austin requires registration under City Ordinance 4.29, and a Change of Ownership form must be filed when a rental is sold. Ask the city whether the same tenants will stay with the new owner, because that decides which form is used.

If you live elsewhere for part of the year, the program also asks you to name a local rental manager who handles emergencies and inspections. Anyone planning to keep the tenants will want to see the rental registration and any inspection results, so pull those documents together before a deal is signed.

Mower County property taxes at closing

Tax bills from Mower County come in two parts, May 15 and October 15, with agricultural second halves due November 15. The Auditor-Treasurer's office is in the Government Center at 201 First Street NE, Suite 7, in Austin, and the phone is 507-437-9535.

  • The county does not mail second-half statements, so a buyer should ask for the amount.
  • Mail payments are judged by postmark, and a private postage meter mark does not count.
  • The county will not accept post-dated checks.
  • A missing statement does not excuse a late payment.

On the deed side, Minnesota Statute 287.21 sets the state deed tax at .0033 of the net consideration when the price is above $3,000. An eCRV is required for sales over $3,000, and a deed cannot pass title while taxes are delinquent. A well statement or well disclosure certificate also has to accompany a transfer deed. Call the Mower County recorder for the local filing steps and fees.

What you must tell a buyer in writing

Before the purchase agreement is signed, Minnesota Statute 513.55 has you put known material facts in writing. It covers facts that could adversely and significantly affect an ordinary buyer's use and enjoyment of the property, made in good faith and to the best of your knowledge. A separate radon statute, section 144.496, adds a written radon disclosure and a copy of the Minnesota Department of Health booklet.

For an Austin house, the facts buyers care about most are basement water, past flooding, roof and furnace age, and any work done without a permit. Writing these down early keeps negotiations short, and it matters even more in a quick sale where the buyer is not hiring an inspector.

A practical order of work: finish the disclosure, gather permits and any rental registration, get the tax amount from the Auditor-Treasurer, and clear any weed or snow charges. With those four done, a cash offer or a listing can move at its own pace without surprises at the table.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need an inspection from the city before selling in Austin?

Ask the building department at City Hall, 500 4th Avenue NE, whether any sale-time step applies to your address. Gather your permits and any rental registration so a buyer can see them.

What happens if I have unpermitted work on my Austin house?

You may be required to remove it, leave it unoccupied or pay for repairs. Ask the building office whether the work can be permitted after the fact before you list.

What are the due dates for Mower County tax?

May 15 and October 15, with second-half agricultural tax due November 15. The county does not mail second-half statements, so request the figure from the Auditor-Treasurer at 507-437-9535 if you need it for closing.

Can a high weed or grass notice block my sale?

Not by itself, but unpaid mowing costs become a special assessment on the parcel. Austin allows 8 inches of grass and gives seven days after notice, so cut it early and ask the clerk for any pending charges.

Is Austin a good place to sell to a landlord or investor?

Often yes. Median rent is $953 and 71.5 percent of homes are owner-occupied, so investors look at the town. A sold rental needs a Change of Ownership form filed with the city.

The quickest exit is usually a cash buyer who takes the place exactly as you leave it. Hiring an agent or selling on your own takes longer, because both lean on open houses and on the buyer's lender signing off.

As the Steele County seat, Owatonna has the recorder, the treasurer and the county finance office all in town. A closing stays simple provided the house has no rental license problems, no delinquent taxes and a clear answer about flooding.

Owatonna housing snapshot

Owners occupy three of every four Owatonna homes. The city sits on both sides of the Straight River, with the oldest neighborhoods on low ground along its eastern side and newer homes along the Maple Creek ravine. Record rain from September 22 to 24, 2010 sent the Straight River and Maple Creek over their banks, and developments built in the floodplains of both streams were completely inundated. Not sure if your parcel lies in a floodplain? The county or the city can tell you.

If your property sits near the river or the creek, write down any water in the basement, drainage fixes or insurance claims you know about before you list. Rental license requirements

Chapter 115 of the city code makes the Fire Department the office where every rental is registered and given a city license. An inspection is scheduled, and the license is issued once the property passes and the fees are paid. A license is valid for two years.

  • Use one application per rental address.
  • File a fresh application the first time a property is rented, once a license runs out, and whenever ownership changes.
  • Renting without a valid license is a misdemeanor, and every day of renting counts as a separate violation.

If your Owatonna house is rented, make sure the license is current before the closing date. A buyer who intends to keep tenants must apply for a new license after the sale. The Fire Department's number is 507-444-2454.

Steele County Recorder fees and the deed tax

The Steele County Recorder charges $46 to record a document and $54 for a well disclosure statement. Mailed or dropped-off documents are turned around in 10 business days or less, and appointments are available during business hours. Splitting a tax parcel costs $100, paid to the county treasurer.

Minnesota sets the deed tax in Minnesota Statutes section 287.21. The rate is 0.33 percent of net consideration above $3,000, collected by the county as the deed is recorded. A transfer with no consideration, or $3,000 or less, pays a flat $1.65.

Before closing, request an itemized settlement statement from the title company that shows the fee, the tax and any unpaid property tax.

Property tax due dates and payment options

Steele County mails real estate tax statements each March, and every owner receives one even if a lender pays the bill. Real estate tax comes due in two installments, May 15 and October 15. If a date lands on a weekend, the deadline moves to the next business day. Agricultural second-half taxes come due in mid-November, and taxes left unpaid at year end become delinquent on January 1.

You can pay at the Finance office inside the County Administration Building, 630 Florence Avenue, send a check to Steele County Finance, P.O. Box 890, or leave it in the drop box out front. The drop box is cleared at 8 a.m. the next business day, and later deposits must include a penalty.

  • A card payment adds 2.5 percent, minimum $1.50.
  • A Visa debit card adds $3.95.
  • E-checks under $10,000 add $1.50.
  • Direct debit carries no fee.

To use direct debit, get the authorization form to the Finance office by April 30 for the first half or by September 30 for the second.

Order of work for a fast Owatonna closing

Begin before you accept anything. Look up your property tax status, because any unpaid balance is taken from your proceeds. For a rental, call the Fire Department about the license. Note any basement water you have seen, and collect receipts for pumps or drainage work. Once an offer comes in, have the closing date, the check amount and the party responsible for each fee put in writing. Next the title company drafts the deed and the settlement statement, and you should expect them to ask for your tax statement and any rental license papers. The Recorder charges $46 to record the deed and $54 for the well disclosure, and the county collects the deed tax at recording. Read the itemized settlement statement before signing and compare each line with the written offer.

What to ask an Owatonna cash buyer

Ask for the offer on paper and read every line.

  • Which party orders the title work and pays for recording?
  • How will the buyer handle past flood or drainage issues in the disclosure?
  • If a rental license is active, who finishes the term?
  • What is the exact payout after deed tax and any county balance?

Also ask whether the buyer will let you stay a few days after closing to finish moving. A direct offer lets you set the move date, and that is its main benefit over a listing. Weigh that against what an open-market sale would leave once repairs and months of upkeep are paid.

Frequently asked questions

Can I hand my Owatonna rental license to the buyer?

No. Ownership changes require a new application, so the buyer applies in their own name. The city issues two-year licenses once an inspection is passed and fees are paid.

What deed tax applies to an Owatonna sale?

The tax equals 0.33 percent of the price once the price passes $3,000, and a sale at or under that amount pays a flat $1.65. The county collects it at the recording stage.

Where can I pay Steele County property tax face to face?

Visit the Finance office on the ground level of the County Administration Building, 630 Florence Avenue, on a weekday. A drop box stands out front by the flagpoles.

What does a well disclosure cost in Steele County?

The recording office charges $54 for a well disclosure statement or certificate. The $46 deed recording fee is separate.

Should I mention the 2010 flood when selling an Owatonna house?

Yes, if your property is near the Straight River or Maple Creek and you know of water damage, mention it. The disclosure covers material facts you know of, and a buyer will look for flood history in that area.

Sell My House Fast in Winona, MN: Options, Costs and Cash Offers

Cash Home Buyers in Minnesota

Sell Your Winona House for Cash

Selling in Winona?
We buy Winona houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

Selling a house in Winona

Winona is a small river city on the Mississippi with a large student population and a lot of rental property. Houses here cost far less than in the Twin Cities suburbs, and the local rules that matter most cover rentals, permits and short-term stays.

Your choices are an agent listing, a private sale, or a cash offer straight from a buyer. The right one turns on how the house is holding up and how quickly you have to be done.

Rentals are the main thing to sort out. With so many student and investor rentals in town, buyers ask early about the license, the date of the last inspection and the tenants' plans. Put the answers on paper and the negotiation moves faster on any route. If the house has always been owner-occupied, the main items are open permits, the basement and the furnace.

Winona housing numbers

The population estimate for July 1, 2025 is 26,530, up 2.1% from 25,997 in April 2020. The city lost people between 2010 and 2020, so the recent gain is a reversal. Figures for 2020 to 2024:

  • 10,786 households averaging 2.13 people
  • 58.0% of homes owner-occupied
  • Median owner-occupied value: $201,800
  • Median gross rent: $882
  • Median household income: $56,337

Sellers tend to be older owners downsizing or heirs settling a parent's house. Buyers are often first-timers or investors. Condition and location set your real price, so ask for a written offer or an agent's estimate first.

Historic district and older houses

Winona was laid out in 1852 and 1853, and much of its housing is old. Two historic districts on the National Register of Historic Places combine into one local historic district under the city's Heritage Preservation Commission. If your house is in that district, ask the city's planning office what review applies before you promise a buyer changes to the exterior.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Winona house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Bluffs, river and weather

Winona is bluff country, hilly, with the river on one side and Lock and Dam 5A across it. Houses face hot humid summers and cold snowy winters. Buyers commonly ask about basements, furnaces and roofs, and about whether a property near the river sits in a mapped floodplain. Ask the city's inspections office or your insurer to confirm the status of your address, and mention any past water in the basement in your written disclosure.

Winona rental license rules

Any rental unit in the city must hold a license before tenants move in, and Chapter 33A of the housing code requires an inspection every five years. When the house you are selling is a rental, expect the buyer to check the license and inspection history.

The licensing steps are short:

  1. Planning and Zoning confirms that the property may be a rental.
  2. The owner submits a rental license application.
  3. The Building Inspections Department inspects the unit.
  4. The fee is paid, due upfront for a new rental.
  5. The property must meet the housing code before the license is issued.

The city also provides a Rental License Transfer of Ownership application, which a buyer of a rental house will need. Call Planning and Zoning at 507-457-8250 to ask whether your property qualifies as a rental, and the inspections office at 507-457-8231 to schedule.

Rental inspection fees

Certification carries an inspection fee once every five years. City Code Chapter 51 sets the amounts, and the current schedule began January 1, 2026.

Winona rental housing inspection fees
Property typeCalculationTotal
Single-family dwelling$100 per unit plus $100 per building$200
Duplex$200 for two units plus $100 per building$300
Owner-occupied duplex$100 for one unit plus $100 per building$200
Sleeping room$45 per room plus $100 per building$145 for one room

In an owner-occupied duplex, the unit the owner lives in isn't certified, so only one unit is charged.

Short-term rentals

A buyer can use a Winona house as a short-term rental only with a license and a public hearing. The city calls these Tourist Homes and defines them as buildings that provide sleeping accommodations to transient guests for up to 29 consecutive days. There are two classes, owner-occupied and non-owner-occupied, each with its own regulations.

  • Every short-term rental needs an inspection and a license.
  • Residential zoning districts require a Planning Commission public hearing before licensing.
  • A 4% hotel and motel tax on monthly rent has applied since July 1, 2018.

If your house has hosted Airbnb-style stays, gather the license paperwork for the buyer. If it hasn't, assume a new owner can't start without the hearing.

Repairs and permits before closing

A building permit is required for additions, alterations, new construction, remodeling and most replacements. Work that needs none includes painting, cabinets, countertops, floor coverings, tiling, storage sheds under 200 square feet, retaining walls up to 4 feet and decks not over 30 inches above grade, unless attached to a permanent structure.

Fences usually need no permit, but ask Planning and Zoning at 507-457-8250 first. Fences may reach 6 feet in the rear and 4 feet on the street side, and anything over 7 feet needs a variance and a permit. The city doesn't issue electrical permits, so electrical questions go to the state electrical inspector. An unpermitted deck or finished basement is something a buyer's inspector will notice, so close out any open permits before you list.

Taxes and paperwork at sale

The county auditor receives a certificate of real estate value for any sale above $3,000, and Minnesota Statutes 272.115 bars homestead status for the buyer if it is missing. The assessor drops the homestead classification after a sale until the new owner applies and qualifies.

The house sits in Winona County, so the deed is recorded with the county recorder there. Ask the county for current recording fees and the deed tax calculation, and have your title company confirm who files the certificate. Minnesota also lets a seller pass the required disclosure to the buyer's agent instead of the buyer directly.

Gather the rental license, permit closeouts and repair receipts before you accept an offer. A cash sale skips the lender and appraisal, so the schedule follows the county paperwork and any rental or permit items, and the buyer takes the house in its current state. With a listing, add showings and the buyer's loan on top. Either way, bring photo ID for every owner who signs and keep copies of the paperwork you gathered, so the title company can close without chasing you for documents.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Does Winona require an inspection before I sell my house?

Winona's inspection program covers rental units, which need a license renewed through an inspection every five years. For a house you live in, ask the inspections office at 507-457-8231 whether anything applies to your address.

How much is a rental inspection in Winona?

A single-family rental costs $200 total, made of $100 per unit and $100 per building, under the schedule effective January 1, 2026. A duplex is $300.

Can I sell a rental house to a new owner in Winona?

Yes. The buyer files a Rental License Transfer of Ownership application, and the property must still meet the housing code. Planning and Zoning at 507-457-8250 can confirm that the property is eligible.

Are Airbnb stays allowed in Winona?

They are allowed with a license. The city treats them as Tourist Homes for stays up to 29 days, requires an inspection and a hearing in residential districts, and charges a 4% hotel and motel tax.

What is the typical home value in Winona?

The median owner-occupied value is $201,800 for 2020 to 2024. Your own number depends on condition and location, so get a written offer or a local agent's estimate before you decide.

Selling a house in Chanhassen: your options

Three paths lead to a closing in Chanhassen: hire an agent, line up your own buyer, or take a cash offer. Prices here run high, which means a staged listing and an as-is sale can land far apart. Ask for both numbers before choosing, and ask what each route would cost you in repairs, fees and carrying costs while the house sits.

  • Agent: best for an updated house when you can host open houses.
  • Private sale: works if the buyer is already known to you, like a neighbor or relative.
  • Cash buyer: fits an estate house, a failing septic system, or a move that cannot wait on a school year or new job.

Owners occupy 84.1% of Chanhassen's homes, so the people a buyer meets on the block are mostly long-term residents rather than tenants.

Chanhassen housing at a glance

Chanhassen is mostly in Carver County, about 15 miles southwest of Minneapolis, with a small eastern piece in Hennepin County. Main roads are U.S. Highway 212 and Minnesota Highways 5 and 41. Chanhassen incorporated as a city in 1967, and the population estimate for July 2025 is 25,748. Lakes such as Lake Ann, Lake Minnewashta and Lotus Lake, plus 70 miles of trails, give listing photos plenty to work with.

Chanhassen housing and income, 2020-2024 unless noted
Housing measureLatest figure
Owner-occupied housing rate84.1%

Median gross rent$1,831 a month

The 2020 rental vacancy rate was 8.5%, a number to weigh when pricing a house that tenants occupy.

Who buys in Chanhassen?

Buyers skew toward established families. The 2020 count found a median age of 40.9, married couples heading 64.9% of households, and children in 36.8% of them. About 90.1% of residents stayed put for a full year, so listings often come from owners with long tenure and substantial equity. Another 15.4% of residents are 65 or older, which feeds a steady supply of downsizers.

If you are selling an inherited house, buyers will hold it up against updated listings at much higher prices. An as-is offer reflects the work the buyer takes on, not the neighborhood's median.

Which school district serves your Chanhassen address?

Most of Chanhassen lies in Eastern Carver County Schools, District 112. Students usually attend Bluff Creek or Chanhassen Elementary, Pioneer Ridge Middle School and Chanhassen High School.

The northern sections belong to the Minnetonka School District, District 276, with students usually going to Clear Springs or Excelsior Elementary, Minnetonka Middle School West and Minnetonka High School. Private options downtown include Chapel Hill Academy and St. Hubert Catholic School. The district line can run through a neighborhood, so ask the district to confirm the address before it goes into a listing.

Septic systems and wells

A parcel that lacks city sewer or water brings extra paperwork. Rural lots most often have private systems, and Minnesota sets two separate disclosures for them.

  • Sewage: before the purchase agreement, you must state in writing whether household sewage goes to a permitted facility or to a subsurface treatment system, and attach any earlier inspection report (Minnesota Statutes section 115.55, subdivision 6). Staying quiet about a known system can leave the seller paying for compliance work if the buyer sues within two years of closing.
  • Wells: you must disclose known wells in writing, and the deed needs a well statement or a certificate with a $54 fee (section 103I.235). Liability for an undisclosed well can run six years from closing.

Carver County treats the subsurface sewage treatment disclosure as required on all property transfers. If you are unsure what is buried in the yard, ask the city's building staff and your title company early.

Short-term rentals before you sell

Chanhassen requires a license for any property rented for fewer than 30 consecutive days, even if it happens only a couple of times a year. The rule took effect January 1, 2023, and ordinary month-to-month leases fall outside it.

The license costs $200 a year, is renewed by February 1, and requires a Minnesota state lodging license. Its terms set the maximum number of overnight guests and vehicles and require compliance with the nuisance ordinance, including a 10 p.m. to 7 a.m. limit on amplified sound. Three notices of violation within 365 days mean revocation, and the owner cannot hold a short-term rental license again for seven years. Neighbors can report problems to a 24/7 hotline at 952-260-4995. If you are listing the house, take down any active short-term listing before the first showing.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Chanhassen houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How Chanhassen deeds are recorded

Most Chanhassen deeds go to Carver County Land Records and Vitals, 600 East 4th Street, Chaska (952-361-1930). The counter runs weekdays 8 to 4:30. Parcels in the Hennepin County sliver are recorded by Hennepin County instead, and your tax statement shows which county applies.

A Carver deed package carries the recording fee, state deed tax, a $5 agricultural conservation fee, a certificate of real estate value for consideration above $3,000, well information, the sewage treatment disclosure, a full legal description, a complete notary acknowledgment, a drafted-by statement and a send-tax-statements-to line. Staff cannot choose a form or give legal advice, so lean on your title company or attorney. The deed tax under section 287.21 is 0.33% of net consideration.

What a buyer will ask you for

Any buyer, cash or financed, will ask for the same short list: the written sewage and well statements, the permit history for big projects, the tax statement showing which county and school district apply, and proof of who holds title. Collect those first. If the house has a septic system, find the last inspection report in your files before you talk to anyone.

A cash buyer subtracts repair costs from the price, so a clear description of known problems helps the offer arrive faster and stay put. When you compare offers, look at the closing date and the conditions as well as the dollar figure.

Timing varies with the file. A clean title and no mortgage can close in a couple of weeks. A payoff, a lien or a recording question on the Hennepin side can add days, so ask the title company which of those apply to you. Once the deed is signed, the title company handles the filing and the county sends the recorded document back.

Frequently asked questions

Will a cash buyer take a Chanhassen house with a septic problem?

Many will, because they buy as is and subtract the repair from the offer. The written sewage disclosure is still yours to provide, along with any inspection report in your files.

Which county records a Chanhassen deed?

Carver County, for almost the whole city. The small eastern portion is in Hennepin County, and your tax statement names the county for your parcel.

Can I run Airbnb stays at my Chanhassen home while it is listed?

Only with the $200 annual city license plus a Minnesota lodging license, since any stay under 30 consecutive days counts. Skip it during showings and avoid the enforcement risk.

What is the deed tax on a Chanhassen sale?

It is 0.33% of net consideration, collected when the deed is recorded. Your title company will show the exact amount on the closing statement.

Which school district covers a Chanhassen address?

District 112, Eastern Carver County Schools, covers most of the city, and Minnetonka's District 276 covers the north. Look up the exact address before advertising a school.

Farmington in brief

Down in southern Dakota County, Farmington marks the metro's outer rim. Population is 25,425, up 7.4 percent since April 2020, spread over roughly 14.6 square miles. Lakeville borders it on the west, and Empire Township lies to the east.

Owners live in 86.5 percent of the housing units, and the middle owner-occupied home is valued at $366,200. Your competition is mostly other single-family houses. The city has 8,313 households of 2.85 people each. Household income sits at $123,673, rent at $1,241 and the drive to work at 27.7 minutes. Monthly owner costs run $2,175 with a mortgage and $781 without, handy numbers if a buyer wonders what the place costs to carry.

County Highway 50 splits the town in two for most residents. The older downtown is south of it, newer subdivisions are north of it, and more growth is spreading east into Empire Township. A trail along the Vermillion River links downtown, uptown and the Empire-side neighborhoods, and deserves a mention in your listing.

Closing your city water account

Before closing, phone Farmington Utility Billing (651-280-6883) and book a final meter reading. Water is not turned off when you move out, so the account runs until you end it.

  • Bills arrive quarterly and cover water, sewer, storm water and street lights.
  • Trash and recycling come from Dick's Sanitation, which takes cancellations at 952-469-2239.
  • An unpaid final bill is certified to the property as a special assessment, and an open account can lead the title company to hold funds back at closing.

Landlords should know that rental utility accounts stay in the owner's name, so the closing falls to you rather than the tenant. Rental accounts that fall behind carry a late fee of 10 percent. Request the exact closing-day balance from Utility Billing instead of relying on the last bill.

Schools and neighborhoods buyers ask about

Farmington is in Independent School District 192, which enrolls about 6,900 students. The attendance area also takes in eastern Lakeville and the surrounding townships, so check which district serves your street before writing the listing.

Condition questions vary by area. Subdivisions north of County Highway 50 are mostly under twenty years old, while downtown houses are older and more likely to need updated systems. Main routes are Minnesota Highways 3 and 50 and Dakota County Roads 31 and 50.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Farmington house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Ways to sell a Farmington house

  • Agent listing: best for a house in good shape, if you can wait through inspections and loan approval.
  • Do it yourself: saves the commission, but you take on marketing, paperwork and negotiation.
  • Cash buyer: suits inherited houses, put-off repairs, rentals with tenants and owners behind on payments. The buyer accepts the house in its present state, and you set the closing date.

On any route, Minnesota Statutes 513.55 has you hand over a written disclosure of known material facts before the purchase agreement. Repairs are not part of that duty. Cash buyers take the house as it stands, while retail buyers often negotiate fixes after an inspection.

Filing the deed in Dakota County

Every Farmington deed goes through the county records office in Hastings. Walk-in filing needs an appointment at the Administration Center, and mailed packets go to 1590 Highway 55 in Hastings with a return envelope. Most parcels countywide are abstract property, so your title company will search the record before closing.

Minnesota's deed tax is the net sale price times 0.0033. The deed must include a well disclosure certificate or a statement that the seller knows of no wells (Minnesota Statutes 103I.235). The auditor also looks for delinquent taxes first (Minnesota Statutes 272.12). Fees come from state law and appear on the county's fee page, and your title company can quote the sum.

Property tax due dates and penalties

Two installments make up the Dakota County bill (Minnesota Statutes 279.01). Miss one and the penalty is 2 percent for a homestead or 4 percent for other property, growing monthly through December.

Dakota County property tax installments
InstallmentDue datePenalty if missed
First halfMay 152 percent homestead, 4 percent other
Second halfOctober 152 percent homestead, 4 percent other

The settlement statement usually divides the year's bill between buyer and seller by closing date. Search your parcel on the county website for open balances before you list. Homestead applications are due December 31.

Owe back taxes? Dakota County Property Taxation and Records can give you the payoff amount. Your latest statement confirms the parcel number and what is already paid.

What about repairs before selling?

The disclosure law does not make you fix the house first. It makes you say what you know. List any leaks, past basement water, aging systems and work in progress, and hand the list over before the purchase agreement. A cash buyer reads the same list and prices around it, so small fixes done only to sell are often wasted effort. A line item you disclose is far safer than one a buyer finds later. If you are selling a house with tenants or a rental history, include the lease terms and any repair requests they made. Photos of recent work, dated receipts, a copy of the survey and a short note on each system's age give buyers confidence and cut down on late haggling.

Gathering what the title company needs

Set out the tax statement, parcel number, lease and keys ahead of time, and for a rental add the utility account details. Most county parcels are abstract property, so the title company will order a search of the record and may ask about old liens or easements. Answer fast, since slow replies push a closing date back. Also tell the buyer about the trail, the school district and anything about the street that affects daily life.

How quickly can a sale close?

With cash, you choose the closing date, and it often lands within a few weeks since no lender appraisal is needed. An agent listing usually takes more time. For either path, schedule the water meter reading in advance and ask the county for your tax payoff figure. On the day, the title company pays off any mortgage and taxes owed, and the deed goes to the records office in Hastings.

Frequently asked questions

How quickly can I close on a Farmington house?

A cash purchase can close on a date you choose, frequently within a few weeks, since no lender appraisal is involved. Listing with an agent generally runs longer. For either path, book the water meter reading with Farmington Utility Billing in advance.

Do I have to make repairs before I sell in Farmington?

No. The disclosure statute asks for a written statement of material facts you know, and repairs are not part of it. Cash buyers take the house as it stands, and retail buyers often negotiate fixes after an inspection.

What happens to an unpaid Farmington utility bill after a sale?

It stays attached to the property. The city certifies unpaid water, sewer, storm drainage and street light charges as a special assessment, so buyers' title companies usually want the last bill settled. A final meter read keeps the number accurate.

Who files the deed for a Farmington sale?

Dakota County's records office in Hastings, normally through your title company. The deed tax is 0.0033 of the net price, and the deed needs either a well certificate or a no-wells statement. The state sets the fees.

Can I sell a Farmington rental while tenants live there?

Yes. Go over the lease terms with the buyer and your title company. Rental utility accounts stay in the owner's name, so plan to close yours on the sale date.

Faribault for home sellers

Faribault is the Rice County seat, about 50 miles south of Minneapolis and Saint Paul, where the Straight and Cannon Rivers meet. Population is 25,040 as of July 2025, up 2.3 percent from 2020. Interstate 35 runs along the western edge, and Minnesota Highways 3, 21 and 60 serve the city.

Owner-occupied houses here carry a typical value of $241,500, and two out of three households (66.1 percent) own their homes. Monthly rent is $1,074. The city counts 8,938 households of 2.48 people each, with income at $61,449 and a drive to work of 19.0 minutes.

Faribault is an older city, and many properties carry decades of ownership history. Ask for the title search and a fresh survey early. Write down when the house was built and when the big updates happened, since buyers always ask and a ready answer keeps things moving.

Repairs against an as-is sale

Prices here are modest, so a big repair eats a large slice of what the house will fetch. A new roof or foundation fix hurts more in Faribault than in a suburb where houses cost two or three times as much. Many owners put the repair bill next to an as-is offer before choosing.

Cold winters mean inspectors go over the roof, gutters and basement with care, so hang on to receipts for recent work. Trails help the pitch too: the Sakatah Singing Hills State Trail starts here and runs to Mankato, and Central Avenue has restored historic storefronts.

What you must disclose in writing

Your basic obligation is in Section 513.55 and reaches every material fact you know about. Radon falls under Section 144.496, wells under Section 103I.235 and sewage under Section 115.55.

Wells come up at the county recorder. A transfer that needs a value certificate also needs well information, and the deed for a lot with no well has to say so. Filing a well disclosure certificate costs $54, and the Health Department's database, or 800-383-9808, shows whether one is already on file.

Keeping it as a rental or letting go

Every residential rental in Faribault must be registered, hold a city rental license and pass inspection. A July 2022 ordinance update ended the requirement that landlords run criminal background checks, though the city still recommends them. It also confirmed an occupancy limit of no less than two times the number of legal bedrooms plus one, with children under age two not counted.

Owners and managers of one or more rental units must hold Crime Free Multi-Housing Phase I certification before a rental license renews. The Building Code Division is at 208 First Avenue NW, phone 507-333-0359, and the rental division takes email at rental@ci.faribault.mn.us.

Training, registration and inspections can be a lot for a house you inherited or left behind. Selling skips all three, and a cash buyer does not ask you to complete them first.

Paying Rice County taxes

Payments go to the Property Tax and Elections Office on the second floor of the Government Services Building, 320 Third Street NW. Bills of $100 or less for the whole year are due in full on the first date.

Behind on taxes? Ask that office for a payoff figure, and your closing agent can settle the balance out of your sale money.

Selling with tenants in place

When renters live in the house, hand the lease to the buyer and the closing agent early. The occupancy limit and inspection rules follow the property, so whoever keeps it as a rental takes over registration and certification. Once the house is empty, let the rental division know. A cash buyer can take the house with tenants still there or after they leave, whichever you agree on.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Faribault houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Recording the deed

Rice County asks for two checks, both payable to the county, when a deed is submitted. One pays recorder fees. The other pays deed tax and mortgage registration tax, which the tax office takes in. The deed tax rate is 0.33 percent (Section 287.21), and the auditor receives the value certificate required by Section 272.115. Reach the recorder at 507-332-6114.

The closing agent usually files the deed. Check your purchase agreement to see who pays each fee.

Your options in Faribault

  • List with an agent: fits a house in good shape when you can sit through showings and wait for a buyer's mortgage.
  • Sell it yourself: you set the price, host the showings and write up the contract.
  • Cash buyer, as is: popular for inherited houses, rentals with open violations and homes whose repairs would outrun what a retail buyer pays.

Get a written estimate from each, then take off commissions, repairs and carrying costs to see your take-home.

Preparing the paperwork

Keep one folder for the sale. Drop in the newest tax statement, a survey if you own one, the well certificate, receipts for roof, furnace or foundation work, and any tenant lease. A title company will want most of it. Inherited the house? Add the court papers showing who may sign.

Then walk through as a buyer would. Jot down every flaw you know of, from a damp basement corner to a sagging gutter, since the written disclosure covers what you know. Inspectors find most of it regardless.

How a cash sale moves

The steps run like this: ask for an offer, let the buyer see the house as it is, then pick a closing day. The title company searches the record, gathers disclosures and drafts the deed. There is no lender appraisal to wait on, and you do not fix anything first. The closing day bends to your calendar, useful if you are leaving town or wrapping up an estate. On closing day you sign the deed, hand over keys and any garage openers, and receive your proceeds once the title company has paid off the mortgage and any taxes owed. Plan a last walk-through so you know the house is empty and the utilities are squared away. Before closing, confirm any well certificate, pay off taxes owed and gather the keys.

Frequently asked questions

How much is a typical house worth in Faribault?

Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $241,500. Condition and street can push yours higher or lower, so use that number only as a rough guide.

Can I sell a Faribault rental that is behind on its license?

Yes. Write or call the city rental division (rental@ci.faribault.mn.us, 507-333-0359) to find out what is open, and tell the buyer about known problems. Anyone who rents the house next must register it and meet the inspection and certification rules.

Who handles recording a Faribault deed?

The Rice County Recorder at 507-332-6114 records deeds, and deed tax is handled by the Property Tax and Elections office. The county asks for separate checks for recorder fees and for deed tax, both payable to Rice County.

Do I need a well disclosure certificate?

If the property has a known well, yes. If you know of no wells, the deed can carry the statement that the seller does not know of any wells on the property. The county charges $54 to file a certificate.

When are Rice County taxes due?

Non-agricultural real property pays on May 15 and October 15, while agricultural parcels pay on May 15 and November 15. A bill of $100 or less for the year is due entirely on May 15.
